title: Five Red X's on the Wall Calendar: Wesley's Perspective on the Morning He Thought He Lost Nate Forever
subtitle: From Fifteen-Year-Old Non-Verbal Wesley Sorenson's Third-Person Limited Point of View — Why Heather's Breakup Felt Like Losing His Only Guy Friend on Earth
location: Chesapeake, Virginia (Wesley's Upstairs Bedroom & Living Room)
recipient: Readers of The Story of Heather Lindstrom & Katie & Nathaniel (Episode 4, Chapter 2)
relatedBookLabel: The Story of Heather Lindstrom — Episode 1, Chapter 1, Part 1: Why Wesley Blew Up
imageAlt: On a sunlit Saturday morning in January 2003 inside his Chesapeake split-level living room, fifteen-year-old non-verbal Wesley Sorenson in a navy-blue fleece quarter-zip pullover and blue jeans with his blue silicone ring on his wrist cradles the oak-framed Emerald Creek Mall snapshot protectively inward against his chest while pointing emphatically toward the closed front door in heartbroken teenage protest, as seventeen-year-old Heather Collins sits stricken on the bottom stair step beside her car keys and his mother Linda watches quietly from the oak bookshelf.
summary: While Katie & Nathaniel follows Nate in Virginia Beach and The Story of Heather Lindstrom follows Heather in Chesapeake, this companion scene enters fifteen-year-old non-verbal Wesley Sorenson's own third-person limited perspective on Saturday morning, January 11, 2003—revealing the sheer terror of having zero phone, bus, or spoken bridge to his very first guy friend when Heather messed up.

toc.text: Saturday, January 11, 2003, 10:40 AM — Five Red Crayon X's & The Only Boy Who Never Talked Baby-Talk

markdown:
> **Archival Note:** In [***The Story of Heather Lindstrom — Episode 1, Chapter 1, Part 1***](https://books.raggiesoft.com/heather/scales-tails-and-safe-people/saturday-pretzel-day-the-empty-shelf-the-boy-without-a-phone-bridge/part-1-the-empty-pretzel-table-the-oak-frame-off-the-shelf-why-wesley-blew-up) and [***Katie & Nathaniel — Episode 4, Chapter 2***](https://books.raggiesoft.com/katie/senior-year-separate-tracks/new-year-s-eve-behind-a-locked-door-the-lie-in-homeroom-212-one-last-pretzel-at-emerald-creek/part-3-tyler-s-parka-lie-blows-up-in-the-cafeteria-five-months-of-silence-signing-up-for-cchr), seventeen-year-old **Heather Collins** ends her relationship with sixteen-year-old **Nathaniel Prairie** outside Room 204 at Northwood High on Monday, January 6, 2003 without letting him speak. Five mornings later, Heather has to tell her fifteen-year-old non-verbal cousin **Wesley** why they aren't driving to **Emerald Creek Mall**. This Backstage companion narrative tells that exact Saturday morning strictly from **Wesley's third-person limited point of view**.

---

## Saturday, January 11, 2003, 10:40 AM — Five Red Crayon X's & The Only Boy Who Never Talked Baby-Talk

Up in his sunlit Chesapeake bedroom, fifteen-year-old Wesley Sorenson uncapped his thick red washable marker, stood right in front of the Puppy-a-Month wall calendar hanging beside his closet door, and drew a careful, triumphant diagonal X across the square for Friday, January tenth.

That left Saturday, January eleventh—the square with the shiny yellow smiley-face sticker his mom had helped him press onto the paper back on New Year's Day.

*Pretzel Saturday.*

Slipping his smooth solid-blue silicone sensory ring over his right wrist and giving the cool rubber two happy squeezes to settle the excited buzz in his fingers, Wesley checked himself in the dresser mirror the way his dad had taught him. Navy-blue fleece pullover zipped halfway up so the collar didn't rub his throat. Clean blue jeans. Both black sneaker laces double-knotted tight so neither loop could trip him on the mall tile.

Downstairs in the foyer, he heard the familiar jingle of Heather's brass keyring.

Wesley loved his big cousin Heather with his whole chest. At school in the self-contained wing, kids in the regular hallways either looked right through Wesley like he was part of the cinderblock wall or slowed their voices down into high, syrupy toddler voices—*Hiiii, Wes-ley!*—even though he was fifteen years old, taller than half the sophomores, and understood almost every single everyday word people said around him as long as they didn't talk three at once.

Nate Prairie had never once used that syrupy voice on him.

From the very first Saturday fourteen months ago when the glass elevator doors had slid open on the second floor of Emerald Creek Mall and two blonde sixteen-year-old twins had rolled out side by side in sleek black power wheelchairs, Nate had looked straight across at Wesley at eye level, held out his right fist, and said, *"Hey, Wes—glad you came. Want half the cinnamon nuggets?"* When the blender at the fruit-smoothie counter shrieked so loud Wesley had to clamp his forearm over his ear and hum low in his throat to keep his head from spinning, Nate hadn't stared or laughed; Nate had calmly reached sideways to hold his sister Katie's hand while Katie did the exact same quiet hum under her breath, and then Nate had slid the biggest, warmest cinnamon-sugar pretzel nugget straight onto Wesley's red tray.

Nate was Wesley's guy buddy. Not a teacher, not a classroom paraprofessional with a lanyard, not a grown-up uncle—Wesley's very first real teenage guy friend on the whole planet.

Eager to beat the eleven-o'clock line at Annie's Pretzels, Wesley bounded down the beige carpeted stairs four steps behind Heather, crossed the living room, and tapped the white front door twice with his flat palm—*pat, pat*—before turning around with his biggest grin and bumping his own knuckles together right in front of his sternum. *Let's go get Nate!*

Except Heather didn't walk to the front door.

Heather stopped halfway down the stairs. Her face looked pale and tight, the way people looked right before a thunderstorm knocked the cable television out, and her fingers stayed wrapped around her car keys instead of reaching for the brass deadbolt.

"Hey, Wes," Heather said in a strange, too-bright voice as she stepped slowly down onto the bottom step. "Listen, bud—you and I can still drive down to Great Bridge for French fries or look at the turtles at the pet shop on Battlefield Boulevard if you want, okay? Just the two of us today."

Wesley blinked. His smile slipped sideways. *Great Bridge?* Nate and Katie didn't go to Great Bridge; the blue-and-yellow bus with the hydraulic front lift dropped Nate and Katie off outside Emerald Creek Mall!

Thinking Heather had simply mixed up which Saturday square they were on, Wesley walked two steps over to the tall oak bookshelf between the front windows and pointed squarely at the wooden five-by-seven frame sitting on the middle shelf—his favorite object in the entire house—showing Katie, Nate, Heather, and Wesley smiling together beneath the white tented mall roof over four red Annie's Pretzels trays. Wesley tapped beside the frame twice, bumped his knuckles together again, and hummed a clear upward question toward Heather. *No, silly—Emerald Creek! Nate and Katie!*

Heather sat down hard on the bottom stair step and let go of her car keys.

"We... we aren't meeting Nate and Katie at Annie's Pretzels today, Wes," Heather said quietly, staring at her jeans before looking up at him. "Nate and I aren't boyfriend and girlfriend anymore. We broke up on Monday. So we won't be hanging out with Nate and Katie anymore."

At first, the words didn't fit together inside Wesley's head.

*Broke up on Monday.* Five whole days ago—all five days Wesley had been drawing red X's on his bedroom wall calendar waiting for Saturday!

*Won't be hanging out with Nate and Katie anymore.*

Wait. Not just today? *Anymore?*

A cold, dizzy drop opened right under Wesley's ribs—the exact terrifying feeling of stepping off a curb in the dark when the pavement wasn't where your sneaker expected it to be. Inside his chest, ten urgent words tried to rush up his throat at the exact same second—*Wait, Nate is MY friend too! Tell Nate I still want to come! Call Nate on the phone!*—and just like every single day of his life, the doorway between his brain and his tongue stayed locked shut, trapping every word behind his teeth where nobody could hear them.

And right behind that locked doorway came the realization that terrified him down to his bones:

*Wesley couldn't call Nate.*

If Wesley picked up the beige corded telephone on the kitchen wall and dialed a number, all the person on the other end would hear were his hums and breaths; strangers hung up when that happened. Wesley didn't know Nate's phone number anyway. Wesley didn't know Nate's street name in Virginia Beach. Wesley couldn't drive a car, didn't have a city bus pass, and wasn't allowed past the end of his own Chesapeake cul-de-sac without an adult or Heather beside him.

Heather was his bridge. Heather was the *only* way Nate even knew where Wesley was—and right now, Nate was probably sitting in his wheelchair in Virginia Beach thinking Wesley didn't want to eat pretzels with him anymore either, all because Heather had messed everything up!

The terror in Wesley's chest caught fire all at once, exploding upward into hot, roaring, helpless anger.

*"AAH—NO! HNN-GH!"*

Wesley flung his left arm straight out toward the closed front door, his throat burning as the loudest shout he had ever let out inside his mom's house echoed off the ceiling. He stayed rooted to his spot on the beige carpet six feet away from the stairs—he would never, ever touch or hurt Heather—yet every muscle in his shoulders shook as hot tears stung the corners of his eyes.

"Wes, wait—please don't yell, it wasn't my fault!" Heather cried from the step, holding both hands out as tears spilled down her cheeks. "Someone at school told everybody that Nate was at a bad party on New Year's Eve, and people in my homeroom were laughing at me, so I had to—"

*"UH-UH! NO!"* Wesley roared right back, shaking his head hard from side to side and stamping his right sneaker straight down into the carpet.

*Bad party? Nate?!* Even at fifteen without spoken sentences, Wesley knew garbage when he heard it! Nate didn't even like loud blenders at the food court! Nate drank ginger ale and apple juice and held Katie's hand whenever strangers bumped their wheelchairs! Heather had listened to mean kids at school instead of listening to *Nate*—and because Heather had messed up, Wesley had just lost his best friend!

Then a second jolt of ice-cold panic shot through Wesley's chest.

On the evening sitcoms Heather watched on television, whenever a teenage girl broke up with her boyfriend, she always marched over to her shelf and ripped up his pictures or threw them in the kitchen trash can.

Spinning toward the oak bookshelf before Heather could even stand up from the stairs, Wesley scooped the five-by-seven wooden frame clean off the middle shelf with both hands, turned the glass strictly inward against the soft navy fleece over his pounding heart so only the brown wooden backing and easel stand faced the room, wrapped his right arm and blue silicone ring protectively across it, and pointed his left hand one last time straight at the front door where Heather's car was parked.

"Wesley, honey, Heather would never touch your picture," his mom said softly and steadily from beside the bookcase, giving him plenty of breathing room. "That frame belongs to you, sweetheart. You can keep it safe in your room."

Wesley didn't trust anybody downstairs with Nate's picture today. Looking once more at Heather sitting small and crying on the bottom step—wanting her to see every bit of how badly she had broken his world—Wesley walked a wide arc around the far side of the stair rail, climbed the stairs two steps at a time with the oak frame pressed tight to his chest, kicked his bedroom door shut with a boom that shook the wall calendar, and sat down on the edge of his bed rocking slowly back and forth with both arms wrapped around his only surviving piece of Emerald Creek Mall.

He didn't know how many Saturdays it was going to take. All fifteen-year-old Wesley knew, setting that oak frame carefully beside his pillow where nobody could ever throw it away, was that he was going to carry that picture back downstairs and tap Nate's face in front of Heather every single weekend until she went back and fixed what she broke.

> **Archival Note:** Because [***Katie & Nathaniel***](https://books.raggiesoft.com/katie) remains strictly inside **Nathaniel Prairie's** lived first-person perspective, Nate only sees the aftermath of senior Homeroom 212 when **Heather Collins** slams her locker door at `8:05 AM` on Monday, January 6, 2003 ([***Episode 4, Chapter 2, Part 2***](https://books.raggiesoft.com/katie/seventeen-senior-year-greenway-court/drunken-new-year/part-2-the-drunken-new-year-lie-heather-s-bitter-goodbye-twin-sisters-always-stay)), glimpses Heather's pale, stricken silence from the true back corner of **Room 204**, across the cafeteria aisle, and across the **Northwood bus loop** from **Stairway A** in [***Episode 4, Chapter 2, Part 3***](https://books.raggiesoft.com/katie/seventeen-senior-year-greenway-court/drunken-new-year/part-3-the-back-corner-of-room-204-a-song-in-my-head-stairway-a), hears her tearful commencement apology beside **Wesley** outside the **Virginia Beach Pavilion** in [***Episode 4, Chapter 2, Part 4***](https://books.raggiesoft.com/katie/seventeen-senior-year-greenway-court/drunken-new-year/part-4-purple-gowns-at-the-pavilion-pomp-and-circumstance-heather-s-apology), and meets Wesley and Heather one final time off **Route 15** at **Emerald Creek Mall** before their family moves back home to Minnesota in [***Episode 4, Chapter 2, Part 5***](https://books.raggiesoft.com/katie/seventeen-senior-year-greenway-court/drunken-new-year/part-5-waiting-by-the-route-15-stop-if-you-walked-away-wesley-s-laminated-buddy-card). This Backstage dossier reconstructs Heather's side of Northwood High School across winter, spring, and June 2003.

---

## 1. Monday, January 6, 2003 (`7:48–8:03 AM`) — What Happened Inside Homeroom 212

When seventeen-year-old **Heather Collins** walked through the front doors of **Northwood High School** at `7:45 AM` on the first Monday back from winter break, she was carrying a holiday tin of homemade peppermint bark in her tote bag—half for **Nate** and half for **Katie**—brought back from her family's holiday trip home to Minnesota outside Saint Paul with **Aunt Linda** and her younger cousin **Wesley** *(and even if Heather and Wesley hadn't left for Minnesota over the holiday, rule-following Nate never would have invited them over on New Year's Eve in violation of David Prairie's strict no-guests house rule)*.

All autumn long, what had made Heather and Nate's relationship so warm was that Heather had never treated Katie like a third wheel. Having grown up fiercely protective of Wesley, Heather had sat on the tan-brown sofa on **Arvin Road** in August 2002, hugged Nate tightly beside Katie, and told him outright that his bond with his twin sister was the most important bond in his life.

Twelve minutes later inside **Senior Homeroom 212**, before the announcements came over the wall speaker, **Tyler** perched on the corner of a front desk in his varsity jacket holding court in front of twenty seniors about the unauthorized New Year's Eve party at **Brittany Fletcher's** cousins' house off Military Highway.

* **Heather's First Instinct (`7:52 AM`):** When Tyler started laughing about how *"wheelchair Nate wedged a chair under a back bedroom doorknob and locked himself inside all night with some girl while the party raged in the living room,"* Heather's immediate reaction was pure loyalty. She looked straight up from her desk in front of the entire homeroom and snapped, *"That was his twin sister Katie, you idiot! Neither one of them drinks, and they were obviously staying away from you guys!"*
* **Tyler's Malicious Escalation & Sleazebag Motive (`7:53 AM` & `Thursday, Jan 9`):** Furious at being called an idiot in front of twenty classmates—and unable to stand watching pretty Heather Collins date *"wheelchair Nate"* instead of him after Nate had shut Katie's bedroom door in his drunken face on New Year's Eve—Tyler ran the **exact same serial sleazebag breakup scam he pulled on every girl with a boyfriend whom he wanted to date**. Looking Heather dead in the eye with a practiced, pitying smirk, he doubled down and lied through his teeth: *"Keep telling yourself that, Collins! His sister wasn't the blonde girl carrying two red cups of vodka punch into that back room before he locked the door on us—everybody in the hall saw them!"* (Three mornings later, on Thursday, January 9, Tyler slid onto the front edge of Heather's homeroom desk smelling of cheap cologne to complete Stage Three of his routine—telling her *"Forget that loser, Collins, let me take you out Friday night so a real guy can treat you right"*—and even though Heather shot him down in disgust on the spot, she was still too proud to stop and question *why* he had wanted her single!)
* **Pride Over Trust (`7:54–8:05 AM`):** Snickers rippled across three rows of desks while two girls in the next aisle looked at Heather with wincing, secondhand pity. Stung to the bone by public humiliation, Heather made the worst mistake of her seventeen years: she let embarrassment in front of strangers override eighteen months of knowing Nathaniel Prairie's character. By the time she stormed out to her locker outside Room 204 at `8:04 AM`, she had tossed the tin of peppermint bark into the hallway trash bin and armored herself in cold fury—cutting off both Nate and Katie before they could get three sentences out and ordering Nate never to speak to her again.

---

## 2. January 8 – February 10, 2003 — Five Weeks Beside Two Empty Wheelchair Spaces

When Heather walked into **Mr. Callahan's** Gold-Day Second-Block Computer Lab (**Room 204**) at `9:09 AM` on Wednesday, January 8, she had steeled herself all morning for an awkward confrontation at the wide front accessible table (`Workstations One, Two, and Three`), where she, Nate, and Katie had earned a `100 / A+` together on December 20.

Instead, she walked in to find two empty spaces of waxed linoleum beside her plastic chair.

Right against the solid cinderblock rear corner wall beside the humming beige server cabinet (`Workstations Thirteen and Fourteen`), Katie and Nate were already logged into their two separate side-by-side CRT workstations so each twin could complete their individual coursework, sitting side by side in their compact black `SwiftChair` power wheelchairs with their inner hands laced together and their eyes fixed strictly on their own glowing screens while rows of classmates worked on essays and browser research ahead of them. Neither twin glared at her, passed notes about her, or complained to mutual classmates. Nate simply took *"Don't ever talk to me again"* at face value and vanished behind a quiet wall of dignity.

What Heather did not know as she stared at her screen at Workstation Three was that Nate didn't need a portable CD player or detention-inducing classroom headphones to drown out the silence of Room 204. Without Nate, Katie, or their father David ever knowing there was a clinical name for it, Nate's mind replayed Track Eight of **Crimson Node's** September 2002 debut album—***"Unhandled Exception"***—in crystal-clear, note-for-note studio fidelity inside his head while Katie (*"Player Two"*) held his hand across the gap between their armrests.

Meanwhile, up at Workstation Three, Heather's righteous anger lasted less than ten school days before an uncomfortable question began gnawing at her stomach:

* **Week 2 (`Jan 13–17`):** Every morning when **Mr. Henderson** and bus aide **Miss Gloria** unloaded **Bus 417** (the short yellow Special Needs lift school bus) at **Stairway A**—closest to the interior B-Wing elevator—every passing period in B-Wing, and every B-Lunch at **Table Twelve** in the Commons, Nate was only ever with Katie.
* **Week 3 (`Jan 21–24`):** Nobody from Brittany Fletcher's crowd ever mentioned a "blonde party girl" again—and Brittany herself looked miserable and hollow-eyed in the hallways after being banned from her Uncle David's house on New Year's Day.
* **Weeks 4 & 5 (`Jan 27 – Feb 10`):** Watching Nate quietly open zip-top bags of dry toasted oat cereal and green cans of ginger ale beside Katie at Table Twelve—the *exact* two things Nate had pleaded that he and Katie were eating behind that locked bedroom door on New Year's Eve—planted a cold, creeping dread in Heather's chest that she was terrified to examine too closely.

---

## 3. Tuesday, February 11, 2003 (`11:48 AM`) — Cousin Hannah's Green Parka & The Gut-Punch Truth

At twelve minutes before noon on Tuesday, February 11, 2003, that dread turned into sickening certainty in less than forty-five seconds.

Sitting at the end of **Table Ten** six feet across the aisle from Katie and Nate's wheelchairs at **Table Twelve**, Heather overheard **Tyler** lean across the adjacent varsity table toward senior girls' soccer captain **Kristen Bauer** using the *exact same lowered, fake-sympathetic voice* he had used in Homeroom 212 on January 6:

1. **The Identical Three-Beat Sleazebag Playbook (`Bait, Double-Down, & Rebound Pitch`):** First, Tyler told Kristen he *"hated to be the guy to tell her"* right before Valentine's Day, claiming he had walked behind the Kempsville Plaza movie theater at `9:30 PM` Saturday night and caught Kristen's boyfriend **Gavin Whitfield** hugging *"some pretty redhead in a forest-green parka"* beside his pickup truck before climbing into the cab together—immediately adding that Kristen should *"dump the zero before Friday and let me take you out for Valentine's Day instead."* When Kristen laughed and called him an idiot—telling him just as Heather had in Homeroom 212 that the girl was family, specifically Gavin's nineteen-year-old maternal cousin **Hannah** (`a student at Virginia Dominion University` who had blown a tire behind the cinema)—Tyler immediately fired the **exact same second-stage double-down lie** that had broken Heather on January 6, scoffing *"Keep telling yourself that, Bauer! I know what Gavin's cousin looks like—that wasn't his cousin! That was some totally different redhead... seriously, ditch him and come out with me Friday night!"*
2. **How Real Trust Sounded & Exposing That Tyler Does This to Every Woman:** Unlike Heather—who had cracked in Homeroom 212 the second Tyler insisted the blonde girl wasn't Katie—**Kristen Bauer and her varsity teammates blew Tyler's entire M.O. wide open** loud enough for four tables to hear: first Kristen nailed his bluff (`Tyler had never met Cousin Hannah in his life, Kristen had helped Gavin's mother pick out that forest-green parka at Emerald Creek Mall, and Kristen had been on three-way speakerphone with Gavin's mother and Hannah while Gavin bolted her spare tire on`), and then her soccer teammates laughed him right out of his seat—calling out that **every girl in the senior class knew Tyler pulled the exact same fake "I saw your boyfriend with another woman" breakup scam on every girl with a boyfriend whom he wanted to date** (`including two girls on varsity track the previous autumn`).
3. **The Last Time Tyler Ever Pulled That Stunt — & His Spring 2003 Pivot to Brittany at Smoker's Corner:** As Tyler slunk toward the dish-return window with his ears burning red, Kristen shook her head in disgust: *"What's sketchy is a total sleazebag making up trashy cheating stories about guys standing next to their own sisters and cousins just because nobody single will go near you! Everybody who actually knows Gavin knows the only women in his life are his mom, his cousin Hannah, and me!"* Getting publicly roasted by the entire Varsity Girls' Soccer team ended Tyler's fake-cheating scam for good—every mainstream girl inside Northwood High treated him like radioactive slime for the rest of senior year. Shut out inside the building, Tyler slunk out past the galvanized fence to **Smoker's Corner** on Macgregory Street, where shunned, guilt-ridden **Brittany Fletcher** (`who had skipped homeroom since New Year's Day and had zero idea what Tyler had done to Nate and Heather`) was cutting class alone—talking her into dropping out right after her eighteenth birthday in March 2003 and beginning the thirteen-year spiral that eventually trapped her in **Hillside Court** public housing in South Richmond (documented in [***Across the James River in Hillside Court***](/books/katie/hillside-court-six-oclock-news-and-holding-the-elevator)).

When Heather's metal spoon slipped from her fingers and clattered onto the cafeteria linoleum, the wave of self-disgust that washed over her made her physically nauseous.

Looking six feet across the aisle at Nathaniel and Katie sitting side by side in their black wheelchairs holding hands over pretzels and ginger ale, every detail—including Tyler leaning on her homeroom desk on January 9 asking to take her out on Friday night—locked together in Heather's mind with merciless clarity. Just as Tyler had doubled down trying to turn Gavin Whitfield's redhead cousin Hannah into *"some totally different redhead"* so he could hit on Kristen Bauer before Valentine's Day, Tyler had taken a two-second hallway glimpse of **blonde-haired Katie** retreating into her own bedroom on New Year's Eve and run his sleazy, copy-paste breakup routine on Heather because he wanted to break them up and date her himself. For five straight weeks across every classroom, hallway, lunch table, and bus loop at Northwood High, **the only woman—blonde or otherwise—anywhere near Nathaniel Prairie's life had ever been his twin sister Katie.** On New Year's Eve, Nate had done everything right: he had refused alcohol, protected his sister behind a locked bedroom door, and stayed completely faithful to her. And in return, because she couldn't bear two minutes of homeroom embarrassment when a serial sleazebag doubled down, she had ambushed Nate at his locker, called him a liar to his face while he begged her to listen, and thrown away eighteen months of trust in sixty seconds.

When Heather half-rose from her bench with tears stinging her eyes to cross the six feet to Table Twelve, Katie calmly met her gaze across the aisle and gave a single, quiet shake of her head while Nate returned his eyes to his transit notebook without looking up.

---

## 4. Spring & June 2003 — Stairway A, Wesley's Anger, & Graduation Day at the Pavilion

Twice over the spring months before graduation—once beside the library return slot in late February and again outside Room 204 on Thursday, April 10, two days after Katie and Nate turned eighteen—Heather stood three steps back from the hallway crowd holding a folded square of notebook paper on which she had written a full, unvarnished apology confessing that she knew Tyler had lied and that Nate and Katie had told her the absolute truth on January 6.

All spring, she never handed that folded paper to him, and she never crossed the covered walkway at `2:05 PM` dismissal to corner his wheelchair.

![At two-oh-five on a sunny April afternoon outside Northwood High School—where the two-story 1992 red-brick building and covered concrete walkway continue from Stairway A past Stairway B toward Stairway C beyond the left edge of the frame—eighteen-year-old twins Katie and Nathaniel Prairie roll side by side in matching black SwiftChair power wheelchairs along the wide concrete sidewalk outside Stairway A toward the lowered right-side hydraulic lift of short yellow Special Needs Bus 417 pulled alongside the unbroken yellow curb, while across the wide asphalt drive lane departing students exiting Stairways A, B, and C walk across the white crosswalk toward the regular yellow school buses parked side by side in their assigned numbered stalls and Heather Collins glances back over her shoulder with quiet sorrow.](https://assets.raggiesoft.com/raggiesoft-books/images/scenes/katie/b004/apr_2003_northwood_stairway_a_special_needs_bus_heather_regular_stalls.jpg)

At Northwood High (which opened in **1992**), afternoon bus dismissal physically mirrored the distance between them: every departing student exited through **Stairways A, B, and C** onto the long covered concrete walkway. Riding the interior elevator down from their separate fourth-block second-floor classes, **Katie and Nate** rolled out onto the wide concrete sidewalk outside **Stairway A** at the head of the walkway. Because there is **no curb ramp** at Stairway A, **Mr. Henderson** pulled **Bus 417**—their short yellow hydraulic-lift Special Needs school bus—right up on the asphalt curb lane **facing Stairway A** so the right-side wheelchair lift bridged over the unbroken yellow curb directly onto the concrete sidewalk, while **Heather** stepped off the covered walkway alongside the students streaming out of Stairways A, B, and C and crossed the wide asphalt drive lane **toward the regular full-size yellow school buses** parked side by side in their **assigned numbered diagonal parking stalls**.

What made those five months between January and June graduation hurt even more at home was **sixteen-year-old Wesley's** reaction from the very first week after Heather screamed at Nate and broke up with him:

* **Wesley's Fury Since January & His Only Photo With Nate:** Having grown up surrounded by Aunt Linda, Heather's mother, and Heather while teenage boys his age either stared or steered wide around him, **Nate was the very first real guy buddy Wesley had ever had in his life**, and Aunt Linda's framed November 2001 snapshot at *Annie's Pretzels* was **the only picture Wesley owned of himself and Nate together**. From the very first Saturday after Winter Break (`January 11, 2003`), when Heather had to admit they weren't meeting Nate and Katie at the mall anymore because she had screamed at Nate and broken up with him, **Wesley was furious with Heather**—taking that framed mall photo off the living-room shelf to hide it in his bedroom so Heather couldn't touch it, and relentlessly demanding through vocalized and non-vocalized cues that Heather go apologize to the twins.
* **Heather's Secret Longing & Nate's Silent Tears:** Every time Heather looked back toward Stairway A at `2:05 PM`, she missed Nate terribly—remembering his shy smile over cinnamon pretzels, his natural kindness toward Wesley, and how safe it had felt hugging him on the **Arvin Road** sofa and out on that December sidewalk. What Heather never saw as Bus 417's folding lift doors closed at Stairway A was the hot, silent tear slipping down Nathaniel's cheek while Katie quietly held his hand across the aisle.
* **Saturday, June 14, 2003 (`Virginia Beach Pavilion` — *Pomp and Circumstance* & One Strictly Bounded Chance for Wesley):** On graduation morning ([***Episode 4, Chapter 2, Part 4***](https://books.raggiesoft.com/katie/seventeen-senior-year-greenway-court/drunken-new-year/part-4-purple-gowns-at-the-pavilion-pomp-and-circumstance-heather-s-apology)), after sitting hopefully through forty minutes of *Pomp and Circumstance*, sixteen-year-old Wesley marched Heather across the Pavilion plaza to Katie and Nate's powerchairs. When Katie and Nate gently told Heather **no** to reforming a romantic relationship right as *Pomp and Circumstance* echoed out of the lobby, **it broke Wesley's heart right in front of them—setting off a lifelong trigger so that graduations forever remained sad events to Wesley**. Seeing innocent Wesley's tears broke the twins' hearts too, and when Heather explained that their family was **originally from Minnesota ("going home" on June 30)** and already planning for Heather to become Wesley's lifelong companion aide, guardian, and conservator (`since Wesley could never be out on his own`), Katie and Nate agreed to one strictly bounded Saturday at **Emerald Creek Mall** strictly for Wesley's sake.
* **Saturday, June 28, 2003 (`Emerald Creek Mall` — Backed Away From the Table, The Last Time in Person, & The Postcard Brandon Trashed):** Two weeks later ([***Episode 4, Chapter 2, Part 5***](https://books.raggiesoft.com/katie/seventeen-senior-year-greenway-court/drunken-new-year/part-5-waiting-by-the-route-15-stop-if-you-walked-away-wesley-s-laminated-buddy-card)), Heather drove Wesley to the **`CVTA Route 15`** stop and sat respectfully backed two feet away from their old corner table with her hands folded in her lap—gently stopping Wesley when he pleaded for her and Nate to hug it out (`even at the end of the afternoon, Wesley still wanted them to hug it out, though it was not meant to be`), publicly taking 100% of the blame when Homeroom 212 classmate **Lauren Mitchell** asked if they were getting back together, and watching quietly as Nate and Katie gave Wesley a miniature toy city bus and a laminated **Buddy Card** printed with their new **Greenway Court** address while **Wesley tried his hardest to understand that moving thirteen hundred miles home to Minnesota meant this would be the last time he ever saw Nate in person**. Across the next year in Minnesota, Wesley and Nate happily traded postcards—until **July 2004**, when **Aunt Linda's medical crisis** turned Wesley's guardianship and conservatorship over to Heather (`shortly before Heather met and started dating her future husband Dan Lindstrom as a package deal with Wesley`) and **Brandon Mercer** intercepted and trashed Wesley's Saint Paul address-update postcard in Williamsburg, cutting off their mail for twelve years while Katie and Nate lay in dark closets wondering if they should have let Heather back in after all.

markdown:
> **Archival Note:** In our [***Minnesota Marriage 'What If' Dossier***](/books/katie/what-if-minnesota-marriage-and-the-unrescued-cousins), **Katie** and **Nathaniel Prairie** relocating thirteen hundred miles north to Minnesota to be with **Heather** and **Wesley** spared the twins from Brandon and Tiffany—at the devastating cost of erasing Katie's Virginia political career and leaving **Cousin Brittany** and **Cousin Chelsea** unrescued.
>
> That raised a heartfelt *"What If?"* question—especially for **Wesley's** sake, since sixteen-year-old Wesley never deserved to lose his very first guy friend through zero fault of his own: **What happens if Nate and Katie accept Heather's apology outside the Virginia Beach Pavilion (or if Heather holds her ground against Tyler's lie in January 2003 so trust is never broken), Heather and Wesley stay in Virginia on in-state college domicile, Katie still becomes a United States Senator, *and* both Brittany and Chelsea come home safe?**

---

## 1. Two Ways Into the Virginia Domicile "What If" (`January 6 Locker` or `June 14 Pavilion`)

Whether trust is preserved on the morning back from Winter Break or mended outside the **Virginia Beach Pavilion** after commencement, the structural foundation of this *"What If?"* timeline leads to the same unbroken four-person Tidewater household:

1. **Variant A — Holding Her Ground Against Tyler's Lie (`Monday, January 6, 2003`):**
   If **Heather Collins** stubbornly stands her ground at her upstairs locker—insisting to **Tyler's** face that the pretty blonde girl in the matching `SwiftChair` who locked a bedroom door with Nate on New Year's Eve *was* his twin sister **Katie** even when Tyler doubles down claiming otherwise (or if **Kristen Bauer's** varsity-table takedown of Tyler's *"mystery redhead behind the Kempsville Plaza movie theater"* lie about Gavin Whitfield's cousin **Hannah** happens right before Winter Break so Heather already knows Tyler's exact script)—trust between Nate, Katie, and Heather is never broken for a single morning. Publicly torched in Homeroom 212, Tyler still retreats to `Smoker's Corner` on Macgregory Street that spring and still traps shunned **Brittany** onto a South Richmond lease by 2013.
2. **Variant B — Accepting Heather's Full-Accountability Apology (`Saturday, June 14, 2003` at the Virginia Beach Pavilion):**
   At `11:52 AM` under the blooming crape-myrtles outside [***Episode 4, Chapter 2, Part 4***](https://books.raggiesoft.com/katie/seventeen-senior-year-greenway-court/drunken-new-year/part-4-purple-gowns-at-the-pavilion-pomp-and-circumstance-heather-s-apology), when sixteen-year-old **Wesley** holds his breath turning his smooth blue silicone ring between both palms after Heather confesses the whole truth without a single excuse, Katie and Nate welcome Heather back on clear calm-communication ground rules—turning *Pomp and Circumstance* into the moment Wesley throws his fist into the air cheering instead of crying, followed by Heather and Nate hugging side by side under the crape-myrtle shade.

---

## 2. Staying in Virginia Under `Code of Virginia § 23-7.4` & Mutual Package-Deal Devotion

Once Nate and Heather are together in June 2003, eighteen-year-old **Heather** and **Aunt Linda** (Wesley's mother) sit down with **David Prairie** around a rock-solid financial and legal reality under **Code of Virginia § 23-7.4** (*Virginia's one-year continuous college domicile statute*):

* **Why Leaving Virginia Costs Thousands:**
  Having lived continuously in Hampton Roads throughout high school, Heather already holds **full Virginia in-state tuition domicile** for the **Community College of Hampton Roads (`CCHR`)** `2+2` Guaranteed Transfer pathway and **Virginia Dominion University (`VDU`)** in Norfolk—whereas uprooting to bounce between states forfeits Virginia domicile, triggers triple out-of-state tuition, and disrupts sixteen-year-old **Wesley's** established Tidewater developmental-services roll right before he turns eighteen.
* **Mutual Package-Deal Devotion (`Two Pairs = One Household of Four`):**

## 3. Summer 2003: The Ten-Campus College Tour for Rising-Junior Wesley (`Zero Crystal Balls`)

   * **`Warwick University` (`WU`, Newport News):** Because Heather drives Aunt Linda's accessible minivan across the Hampton Roads Bridge-Tunnel, Katie and Nate still have zero Peninsula bus-transfer knowledge of their own while admiring the sunny Neo-Georgian colonnades and watching a blue-and-silver CVTA coach exit the `SR-312 & Shoe Lane` roundabout displaying <led>112 NNTC</led>.

markdown:
> **Cross-Book Continuity Note:** Across the shared Tidewater universe of Ocean View Archives, the **Delores Mahone** who corners **Jack Bennett** during a January 2007 campus open house at **Virginia Dominion University (`VDU`)** in [***Jack & Sarah***](https://books.raggiesoft.com/jack-sarah) is the **exact same Delores** who isolated **Leo Porter** in Portsmouth three years earlier in [***Luna & Leo***](https://books.raggiesoft.com/luna-leo).
>
> Because those two novels share a single timeline, changing how **Luna** and **Stella Porter** react during the hijacked **October 2003 Columbus Day Sibling Weekend** ([***Luna & Leo — Era 12, Chapter 3, Part 2***](https://books.raggiesoft.com/luna-leo/the-delores-nightmare/the-hijacked-plan/part-2-printer-rage-guardianship-questions-and-the-flute-signal)) doesn't just transform *Luna & Leo*—it sends a direct psychological and financial knock-on effect straight into **Robyn and Delores Mahone's** January 2007 dinner table in [***Jack & Sarah — Era 2, Chapter 8***](https://books.raggiesoft.com/jack-sarah/jack-and-delores/an-unassuming-dinner-the-debrief/an-unassuming-dinner-the-debrief).

---

## 1. `Saturday, October 11, 2003, 5:10 PM` (*Luna & Leo*): Luna Screams *"GET OUT!"*

From the moment **Stella Porter** pulled her Holt Sentinel up to the Portsmouth apartment on Friday afternoon, October 10, 2003, the three-day holiday weekend was supposed to be one simple, sacred thing: **a Sibling Weekend—a brother, his twin sister Luna, and his older sister Stella**.

Instead, **Delores** invited herself along unasked, claimed Leo's front passenger seat, mocked the dual `MagnaByte Opus` computer desk, vetoed the Elizabeth River Trail, hovered suspiciously outside Leo's daily speakerphone call with **Olivia Walker** in Montréal, shrieked like a siren over the *ZZZT-CHUNK* of their `MagnaByte GraphiPrint` dot-matrix tractor printer, "sweetly" suggested to Stella's face that Stella hand Leo's court-appointed **Guardianship and Conservatorship** over to Delores, and snapped at Luna for humming the twin distress flute passage from **Fractured Prisms's** *Kaleidoscope Sun*.

In the mainline novel, when Delores rises from the sofa at `5:10 PM` and clamps both hands around Leo's forearms to yank him out of his wheelchair onto her lap, Luna and Stella freeze—terrified that screaming at Delores in Virginia Beach will bring worse retaliation down on Leo behind a locked apartment door back in Portsmouth.

**In this *"What If?"* timeline, the dam behind Luna's ribs shatters half a heartbeat *before* Delores can lift Leo an inch:**

* **The Explosion in Stella's Living Room:**
  Luna's wooden desk chair crashes backward onto the carpet behind the `MagnaByte` desk. Crossing the living room in three furious strides, Luna plants herself squarely between Delores and her twin brother's footrests and screams ***"GET OUT!"*** at the top of her lungs:
  > *"Don't you DARE put your hands on my brother! This was supposed to be OUR weekend! Just Leo, me, and Stella! You invited yourself into our car, you stole his front seat, you insulted our house, you screamed at our printer, you tried to keep him off the phone with his best friend, and now you think you can grab him out of his chair right in front of us?! GET OUT OF OUR HOUSE!"*
* **Stella Drops the Legal Hammer & Leo Clicks His Brakes:**
  Expecting measured older sister Stella to scold Luna and smooth things over, Delores demands that Leo grab his backpack to leave with her. Instead, Stella dries her hands on a dish towel, walks out of the kitchen to stand shoulder to shoulder beside Luna, carries Delores's canvas overnight bag four paces to the front door, and sets it squarely out on the concrete porch stoop—invoking the exact Virginia Circuit Court plenary guardianship and conservatorship order Delores was questioning five minutes earlier to terminate Leo's Portsmouth living arrangement **permanently on the spot**. Behind his two sisters, Leo clicks both manual wheel locks tight with his own hands and types two unmistakable words on his Quantum Communicator: <aac>Go away.</aac>
* **Reclaiming the True Three-Sibling Weekend (`Oct 11–13, 2003`):**
  With the brass deadbolt and security chain locked behind a furious Delores storming toward the Saturday `CVTA` corner stop—and Delores **never welcomed back into Leo's life**—the Columbus Day weekend becomes exactly what it was meant to be: a brother, his twin sister, and his older sister ordering hot extra-cheese pizza, spinning Stella's **Fractured Prisms** vinyl LPs (*...And Only Three Remained...* and *Kaleidoscope Sun*), decompressing in Luna and Leo's safe L-shaped sofa embrace, and sharing an unhurried, joyful two-hour speakerphone call with **Olivia** in Montréal.

---

## 2. `Oct 2003 – Sep 2004` (*Luna & Leo*): Zero Four-Day Pathfinder Trip to Washington State

Throwing Delores out on October 11, 2003 erases the darkest arc of *Luna & Leo* before it can ever happen:

1. **Tuesday Morning Portsmouth Civil Standby (`October 14, 2003`):**
   Instead of Leo enduring a grueling multi-bus Tuesday morning ride back into Portsmouth captivity, Leo stays safe in Virginia Beach with Luna and **Grandma Eleanor** while **Stella and Grandpa Arthur** cross the Midtown Tunnel accompanied by a uniformed **Portsmouth Police civil-standby officer**—packing every textbook, `MagnaByte` floppy disk, charger, and sweater out of **Robyn and Delores Mahone's** apartment in twenty minutes flat and serving formal written notice that any contact will be met with an immediate protective order.
2. **No `$99` Pathfinder Bus Ordeal to Kent, Washington (`November 2003`):**
   Because Delores no longer has access to Leo or his monthly support funds, **the four-day cross-country Pathfinder bus trip from Virginia to Aunt Carol's apartment in Kent, Washington never happens**—meaning zero confiscated or smashed AAC device, zero four-day neglect injuries or hospitalization, zero frantic airport TTY collect call from Sea-Tac, and zero emergency Flight 1138 rescue.
3. **Olivia's Return & September 17, 2004 Without a Courtroom Trial:**
   Leo celebrates Thanksgiving and a Québec poutine *Réveillon* whole and uninjured in Virginia Beach, enrolls alongside Stella, Luna, and newly arrived **Olivia Walker** in *Beginning French I* at `CCHR` in January 2004, and rolls into Virginia Beach Circuit Court on **September 17, 2004** strictly for the joyful half of that date—celebrating Olivia legally taking the name **Olivia Walker Porter** before moving north to their gated coastal sanctuary in **Iron Point, Rhode Island**, with zero `$8,745` restitution lawsuit needed.

## 3. `January–March 2007`: The Knock-On Effect in *Jack & Sarah*

Three years later, in **January 2007**, twenty-something **Delores Mahone** is taking classes at **Virginia Dominion University (`VDU`)** when kind-hearted Fairlawn Recreation Center staffer **Jack Bennett** attends a campus tour ([***Jack & Sarah — Era 2, Chapter 7***](https://books.raggiesoft.com/jack-sarah/jack-and-delores/a-cousin-s-rescue-conversations-on-a-ride-home)).

Because Delores's manipulative personality hasn't changed an ounce—she still spins the exact same inverted victim script at the Fairlawn front desk claiming she *"just got out of a really controlling relationship"*—Jack, his sister **Sarah**, and his twin cousins **Molly and Clare** still form their unbreakable four-person protective wall around him. **Beneath the surface, however, throwing Delores out during the October 2003 Sibling Weekend reshapes three pivotal moments in *Jack & Sarah*:**

### A. Why Robyn Mahone Is Furious Over the ValueMart Freezer Lasagna (`Jan 27, 2007`, `e002/c008/p001.md`)
In mainline *Jack & Sarah*, when Molly drives Jack to Delores and **Robyn Mahone's** apartment for Robyn's "world-famous" ValueMart freezer-lasagna dinner, Robyn's passive-aggressive jabs at Delores stem from screaming phone calls from Aunt Carol in Washington and the massive, unpayable `$8,745+` court restitution debt Delores owes the Porter family.

**In the Sibling Weekend Throwout timeline, Delores owes zero Washington court debt—yet Robyn is every bit as livid at her daughter for the opposite financial reason:**
* Robyn is still seething over the mortifying Tuesday morning when Stella and Arthur Porter showed up at her Portsmouth door with a **uniformed police officer** in front of the whole apartment building—and over how Delores's reckless temper **blew their golden meal ticket with the wealthy Porter family**, costing Robyn the steady household rent share Leo's placement had brought in.
* When Robyn stares creepily across the dining table at Jack and purrs about knowing his newly divorced father **Jermaine Bennett** from work, she isn't looking for someone to pay off a Washington judgment; she is sizing up Jermaine as the **replacement meal ticket** to make up for the Porter windfall Delores squandered.

### B. Delores's Heart Hospital Scream (`e003/c002/p001.md`) & Final Retreat (`e003/c008/p001.md`)
* **Outside the Hospital (`e003/c002/p001.md`):** When Sarah, Molly, and Clare block Delores from isolating Jack during the family medical scare, Delores's mask slips and betrays the exact wound festering inside her since October 11, 2003:
  > *"I had Leo right where I wanted him! Completely under my thumb, and his precious sisters threw me out and ruined everything! I will NOT let you people do it to me again with Jack!"*
* **The Final Wall (`e003/c008/p001.md`):** When all four Bennetts confront her together, Delores backs down remembering Stella Porter's ice-cold porch warning of a Virginia Beach protective order and the uniformed Portsmouth police standby.

### C. A Deeper Psychological Lock on *"The Biological Deadline"* (`e003/c009/p002.md`)
Most strikingly of all, the Sibling Weekend throwout makes Sarah and Molly's deduction in **Era 3, Chapter 9 (*"The Biological Deadline"*)** click into place with chilling precision:
* Why did Delores lead Jack into a pitch-black VDU Chemistry hallway and an empty apartment bedroom to initiate an unguarded sexual encounter **within hours of meeting him** during her fertile window?
* Because in October 2003, **Stella Porter's legal guardianship** allowed Leo's sisters to scream *"GET OUT!"*, put Delores's bag on the porch stoop, and erase Delores from Leo's life in sixty seconds flat because Delores had **zero legal or biological tie** to him. Determined never to let another protective sister (`Sarah`) or twin cousins (`Molly and Clare`) throw her off a porch again, Delores was racing on Day One to manufacture an instant biological anchor that no family wall could ever legally sever.

---

## 4. Cross-Book Comparison Summary (`Mainline` vs. `Sibling Weekend Throwout 'What If'`)

| **Jan 27, 2007 (`Jack & Sarah` Lasagna Dinner)** | Robyn fumes over Aunt Carol's calls & Delores's unpayable Washington restitution debt | Robyn fumes over the Portsmouth police standby & **Delores blowing the wealthy Porter meal ticket** |

markdown:
> **Archival Note:** In [***Katie & Nathaniel — Episode 5, Chapter 1, Part 2***](https://books.raggiesoft.com/katie/six-buses-from-williamsburg-sea-breeze-west-coming-home-to-arvin-road/north-henry-street-six-buses-from-williamsburg-the-goyeau-street-tunnel-file/part-2-six-buses-from-williamsburg-the-blind-leap-at-boundary-street-crown-burger-open-radio-on-route-20-dad-at-indian-river-road) and [***Part 3***](https://books.raggiesoft.com/katie/six-buses-from-williamsburg-sea-breeze-west-coming-home-to-arvin-road/north-henry-street-six-buses-from-williamsburg-the-goyeau-street-tunnel-file/part-3-the-goyeau-street-tunnel-bus-the-trashed-ticket-on-east-jefferson-avenue-protected-non-traveling-complainant), readers watch nineteen-year-old twins Katie and Nathaniel Prairie take a blind leap of faith onto the 4:00 PM CTTA Grey Line bus outside the Williamsburg Transportation Center on Saturday, October 16, 2004—riding six buses across two transit agencies to meet their father David Prairie at Military Highway and Indian River Road at 8:01 PM—and then accompany David to the Walter E. Hoffman United States Courthouse on Granby Street in Norfolk four days later. This Backstage dossier reconstructs what happened in between from the perspective of the Williamsburg Police Department, the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA), U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), and the United States Marshals Service.

---

## 1. Saturday Afternoon & Night, October 16, 2004 (3:52 PM – 11:30 PM): The Blind Ticket Counter at 468 North Boundary Street

When twenty-two-year-old Brandon Mercer ordered nineteen-year-old Katie and Nate to wait outside by the bus bays of the Williamsburg Transportation Center while he stepped inside the historic red-brick depot, he walked up to an interior American Rail Transit System (ARTS) ticket counter with zero window line of sight to the bus bays outside.

1. **Two Full-Price, Non-Refundable Regular Adult Tickets to Detroit:**
   Because Brandon had never ridden public transit with disabled riders, he had no idea ARTS offered discounted *Passenger with a Disability* and companion tariffs. Instead, he emptied nearly his entire checking account (leaving $4.12 on his station ATM receipt) to pay cash for two full-price, non-refundable Regular Adult one-way rail-and-thruway tickets to Detroit, Michigan—intending to haul Katie across the river into Ontario for a "fresh start" and abandon Nate stranded on the Williamsburg platform once the train pulled in.
2. **Why Brandon Booked Detroit + Tunnel Bus Instead of Cross-Border Rail:**
   Hidden inside a lockbox at the house off North Henry Street were two external hard drives containing skimmed resort front-desk credit-card magnetic-stripe dumps and stolen guest identity profiles. Afraid that booking a direct cross-border ARTS train into Ontario would transmit his name on an advance electronic passenger manifest hours before reaching the border, Brandon convinced himself that riding domestically to Detroit and walking onto a municipal Transit Windsor Tunnel Bus would let him slip quietly into Canada and sign up for free Ontario Health Insurance Plan (OHIP) coverage.
3. **Walking Out to an Empty Brick Bus Island (4:02 PM):**
   When the manual multi-segment paper ticket jacket finished printing and Brandon pushed back out the double doors, both SwiftChair powerchairs were gone—already rolling southeast onto U.S. Route 60 (Pocahontas Trail) toward Newport News aboard the 4:00 PM CTTA Grey Line to Lee Hall. Realizing Katie and Nate were heading straight to David Prairie and the police—and furious at the thought of eating two expensive, non-refundable Regular Adult tickets—Brandon hurried two blocks back toward North Henry Street, stuffed his clothes and both contraband hard drives into a fifty-pound canvas duffel bag, and boarded the evening northbound ARTS train toward Washington, Toledo, and Detroit using his own valid Regular Adult ticket.

---

## 2. Sunday Afternoon, October 17, 2004 (3:45 PM – 4:50 PM): East Jefferson Avenue, The Tunnel Bus Farebox, & 555 Goyeau Street / 35 Park Street East

Stepping off his connecting thruway coach in downtown Detroit, Michigan on Sunday afternoon after twenty hours without sleep, Brandon walked down toward the Detroit-Windsor Tunnel plaza at East Jefferson Avenue and Randolph Street—and made three consecutive blunders before he even reached a Canadian border podium:

* **Ripping Up Katie's Unused Ticket on East Jefferson Avenue (3:50 PM):**
  Furious every time he looked at Katie's unused Regular Adult voucher inside the yellow ARTS ticket jacket, Brandon tore Katie's ticket and the attached purchase receipt in half and threw both into a municipal trash barrel on East Jefferson Avenue—unknowingly destroying the unused ticket's residual exchange value that could have paid his bus fare back to Virginia.
* **The Transit Windsor Farebox Surprise (4:00 PM):**
  Boarding the cross-border Transit Windsor Tunnel Bus, Brandon discovered that Transit Windsor accepted U.S. currency strictly at a one-to-one par rate rather than giving an exchange premium, that the Canadian electronic coin validator rejected American dimes and American gold-colored one-dollar coins (because Canadian dimes use a different metallic composition and Loonies have a distinct eleven-sided signature), and that municipal fareboxes issue zero change. Forced to shove his very last ten-dollar U.S. bill into the exact-fare slot to pay a single tunnel fare, Brandon rode under the Detroit River into Ontario with $1.75 in spendable American cash left in his pocket.
* **Refusal of Entry at 555 Goyeau Street & 35 Park Street East (4:15 PM – 4:50 PM):**
  Emerging onto the Canadian inspection plaza at 555 Goyeau Street (near Wyandotte Street East), all Tunnel Bus passengers were directed inside the CBSA Windsor Tunnel District Operations building at 35 Park Street East. Referred to Secondary Inspection by CBSA Officer Vance after snapping that as an American citizen with a birth certificate he had a "right" to enter Canada, Brandon had his duffel bag unpacked on the steel inspection table—revealing his birth certificate folder, $1.75 in spendable cash, his $4.12 Williamsburg ATM slip, two external hard drives, and three pages of printed internet notes about moving permanently to Ontario and signing up for OHIP. Informed that American tourists have zero legal right to reside in Canada or receive provincial healthcare, Brandon was formally refused entry under Sections 20 and 39 of Canada's *Immigration and Refugee Protection Act* and—after lunging at the counter in an outburst—driven back through the tunnel in a custodial CBSA return transfer.

---

## 3. Sunday Evening to Tuesday (October 17–19, 2004): The CBP Contraband Seizure on Randolph Street & The U.S. Marshals Arrest on Cass Avenue

At 5:05 PM on Sunday evening, CBSA officers escorted Brandon straight through the security door of the U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) compound at East Jefferson Avenue and Randolph Street in Detroit:

1. **Mandatory Warrantless Border Search (19 U.S.C. § 1582):**
   Conducting a routine border examination of a foreign-refused traveler, Detroit CBP officers powered on the two external hard drives in Brandon's duffel bag—uncovering hundreds of skimmed credit-card magnetic-stripe dumps and stolen guest identity files from Williamsburg hospitality registers, instantly elevating Brandon's local misconduct into a multi-count federal wire-fraud and identity-theft prosecution.
2. **Arrested Outside the Men's Shelter on Cass Avenue (Tuesday, October 19, 2004):**
   Released onto Randolph Street with $1.75 in spendable cash while CBP forensic agents transmitted the seized drive images to federal prosecutors in Virginia and Michigan, Brandon walked nine blocks northwest to a brick men's homeless shelter on Cass Avenue—where Deputy United States Marshals arrested him on federal felony warrants without incident.
3. **Protected Non-Traveling Complainant (V-W, Zero Infraction) (Wednesday, October 20, 2004):**
   Because the Williamsburg station security camera and ARTS ticket audit proved Katie never boarded the train and escaped six hundred miles away while Brandon destroyed her unused ticket himself on East Jefferson Avenue, Special Agent Morales at the Walter E. Hoffman U.S. Courthouse on Granby Street confirmed that Katie's name carried a permanent *Protected Non-Traveling Complainant (V-W, Zero Infraction)* shield—certifying zero criminal, civil, or immigration infractions in both U.S. and Canadian databases for life.

Instead, he emptied nearly his entire checking account (leaving $4.12 on his station ATM receipt) to pay cash for two full-price, non-refundable Regular Adult one-way rail-and-thruway tickets to Detroit, Michigan—intending to haul Katie across the river into Ontario for a "fresh start" and abandon Nate stranded on the Williamsburg platform once the train pulled in.
  2. Why Brandon Booked Detroit + Tunnel Bus Instead of Cross-Border Rail:
    Hidden inside a lockbox at the house off North Henry Street were two external hard drives containing skimmed resort front-desk credit-card magnetic-stripe dumps and stolen guest identity profiles. Afraid that booking a direct cross-border ARTS train into Ontario would transmit his name on an advance electronic passenger manifest hours before reaching the border, Brandon convinced himself that riding domestically to Detroit and walking onto a municipal Transit Windsor Tunnel Bus would let him slip quietly into Canada and sign up for free Ontario Health Insurance Plan (OHIP) coverage.
  3. Walking Out to an Empty Brick Bus Island (4:02 PM):
    When the manual multi-segment paper ticket jacket finished printing and Brandon pushed back out the double doors, both SwiftChair powerchairs were gone—already rolling southeast onto U.S. Route 60 (Pocahontas Trail) toward Newport News aboard the 4:00 PM CTTA Grey Line to Lee Hall. Realizing Katie and Nate were heading straight to David Prairie and the police—and furious at the thought of eating two expensive, non-refundable Regular Adult tickets—Brandon hurried two blocks back toward North Henry Street, stuffed his clothes and both contraband hard drives into a fifty-pound canvas duffel bag, and boarded the evening northbound ARTS train toward Washington, Toledo, and Detroit using his own valid Regular Adult ticket.

2. Sunday Afternoon, October 17, 2004 (3:45 PM – 4:50 PM): East Jefferson Avenue, The Tunnel Bus Farebox, & 555 Goyeau Street / 35 Park Street East

Stepping off his connecting thruway coach in downtown Detroit, Michigan on Sunday afternoon after twenty hours without sleep, Brandon walked down toward the Detroit-Windsor Tunnel plaza at East Jefferson Avenue and Randolph Street—and made three consecutive blunders before he even reached a Canadian border podium:

  • Ripping Up Katie's Unused Ticket on East Jefferson Avenue (3:50 PM):
    Furious every time he looked at Katie's unused Regular Adult voucher inside the yellow ARTS ticket jacket, Brandon tore Katie's ticket and the attached purchase receipt in half and threw both into a municipal trash barrel on East Jefferson Avenue—unknowingly destroying the unused ticket's residual exchange value that could have paid his bus fare back to Virginia.
  • The Transit Windsor Farebox Surprise (4:00 PM):
    Boarding the cross-border Transit Windsor Tunnel Bus, Brandon discovered that Transit Windsor accepted U.S. currency strictly at a one-to-one par rate rather than giving an exchange premium, that the Canadian electronic coin validator rejected American dimes and American gold-colored one-dollar coins (because Canadian dimes use a different metallic composition and Loonies have a distinct eleven-sided signature), and that municipal fareboxes issue zero change. Forced to shove his very last ten-dollar U.S. bill into the exact-fare slot to pay a single tunnel fare, Brandon rode under the Detroit River into Ontario with $1.75 in spendable American cash left in his pocket.
  • Refusal of Entry at 555 Goyeau Street & 35 Park Street East (4:15 PM – 4:50 PM):
    Emerging onto the Canadian inspection plaza at 555 Goyeau Street (near Wyandotte Street East), all Tunnel Bus passengers were directed inside the CBSA Windsor Tunnel District Operations building at 35 Park Street East. Referred to Secondary Inspection by CBSA Officer Vance after snapping that as an American citizen with a birth certificate he had a "right" to enter Canada, Brandon had his duffel bag unpacked on the steel inspection table—revealing his birth certificate folder, $1.75 in spendable cash, his $4.12 Williamsburg ATM slip, two external hard drives, and three pages of printed internet notes about moving permanently to Ontario and signing up for OHIP. Informed that American tourists have zero legal right to reside in Canada or receive provincial healthcare, Brandon was formally refused entry under Sections 20 and 39 of Canada's Immigration and Refugee Protection Act and—after lunging at the counter in an outburst—driven back through the tunnel in a custodial CBSA return transfer.

3. Sunday Evening to Tuesday (October 17–19, 2004): The CBP Contraband Seizure on Randolph Street & The U.S. Marshals Arrest on Cass Avenue

At 5:05 PM on Sunday evening, CBSA officers escorted Brandon straight through the security door of the U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) compound at East Jefferson Avenue and Randolph Street in Detroit:

  1. Mandatory Warrantless Border Search (19 U.S.C. § 1582):
    Conducting a routine border examination of a foreign-refused traveler, Detroit CBP officers powered on the two external hard drives in Brandon's duffel bag—uncovering hundreds of skimmed credit-card magnetic-stripe dumps and stolen guest identity files from Williamsburg hospitality registers, instantly elevating Brandon's local misconduct into a multi-count federal wire-fraud and identity-theft prosecution.
  2. Arrested Outside the Men's Shelter on Cass Avenue (Tuesday, October 19, 2004):
    Released onto Randolph Street with $1.75 in spendable cash while CBP forensic agents transmitted the seized drive images to federal prosecutors in Virginia and Michigan, Brandon walked nine blocks northwest to a brick men's homeless shelter on Cass Avenue—where Deputy United States Marshals arrested him on federal felony warrants without incident.
  3. Protected Non-Traveling Complainant (V-W, Zero Infraction) (Wednesday, October 20, 2004):
    Because the Williamsburg station security camera and ARTS ticket audit proved Katie never boarded the train and escaped six hundred miles away while Brandon destroyed her unused ticket himself on East Jefferson Avenue, Special Agent Morales at the Walter E. Hoffman U.S. Courthouse on Granby Street confirmed that Katie's name carried a permanent Protected Non-Traveling Complainant (V-W, Zero Infraction) shield—certifying zero criminal, civil, or immigration infractions in both U.S. and Canadian databases for life.

summary: Uncovers the two behind-the-scenes operations shielding David Vance between Thanksgiving night and Christmas Eve 2004: how Wendy Vance, the Virginia Beach Delaneys, and Cassandra's legal firewall intercepted Kristine's three-week campaign to ambush David during community college finals, and how the Bouchard and Delaney families permitted the 6:00 PM Mussel Bed Shoal Road closure beneath the Mount Hope Bridge.

markdown:
Between [***Book 2, Chapter 9: "The Twenty-One Day Bridge & The Birthday Buyout"***](https://books.raggiesoft.com/quantum-directive-3-casey/book-2-the-sovereign-perimeter/chapter-9-the-crossroads/part-2-the-twenty-one-day-bridge-the-birthday-buyout) (`November 25, 2004`) and [***Chapter 16: "The Morning Pile & The House Guard Marathon"***](https://books.raggiesoft.com/quantum-directive-3-casey/book-2-the-sovereign-perimeter/chapter-16-the-aquidneck-christmas/the-morning-pile-the-house-guard-marathon) (`December 24, 2004`), nineteen-year-old **David Vance** experiences three quiet weeks finishing his fall community college exams in Virginia Beach, flies first-class to Seattle with **Elizabeth "Liz" Carter** on December 17, discovers Cassandra's newly purchased Redmond home, and steps onto Mussel Bed Shoal Road in Portsmouth, Rhode Island to find a warm Québécois **Réveillon** block party glowing underneath the **Mount Hope Bridge**. Because the pack deliberately insulated David's bandwidth so he could keep his `3.5` GPA intact, David never sees the three-week interception perimeter holding **Kristine** at bay—or the Town Hall logistics required to move a traditional midnight French-Canadian feast up to `6:00 PM` beneath a suspension bridge in December. --- ## 1. Holding the Line During the Twenty-One-Day Finals Bridge (`Nov 26 – Dec 16, 2004`) Kristine assumed David's Thanksgiving afternoon walkout was a temporary tantrum engineered by his sisters—and that once **Cassandra** and seventeen-year-old **Casey** boarded their Sunday flight back to Sea-Tac on **November 28**, David's caretaking guilt would pull him straight back to Portsmouth, Virginia. At `7:45 PM` on Sunday evening—less than two hours after Cassandra's flight pushed back from Norfolk International—the Vance landline rang in Virginia Beach while David was upstairs reviewing anatomy flashcards with **Morgan** and **Meredith Delaney**. **Wendy Vance** picked up the kitchen extension before the second ring finished. On the other end of the line, Kristine didn't sound angry; she deployed the exact fragile, tear-choked register that had overridden David's threat detection for six months, claiming she had suffered a panic attack alone in the apartment and needed David to drive over *"just for twenty minutes"* to help her calm down. Wendy didn't raise her voice, and she didn't call upstairs. Having raised three neurodivergent children—and having listened to Cassandra's glacial debriefing on Thursday afternoon—Wendy spoke with quiet, immovable finality. "David is studying for his finals, Kristine, and he no longer lives at that address," Wendy said evenly. "Everything belonging to him was removed on Thursday. Do not call this house again, and do not approach him on campus." When Kristine pivoted forty-eight hours later—driving across the Elizabeth River on Tuesday morning to stake out the student drop-off loop at the **Community College of Hampton Roads**—she discovered why Meredith Delaney had promised David he wouldn't spend a single second of those twenty-one days unguarded. * **Campus Escort Rotation:** Every morning and afternoon between November 29 and December 15, either **Morgan** or **Meredith** walked David door-to-door from the Delaney minivan directly to his classroom threshold and waited outside the hall during exam blocks. Spotting the six-foot-two Morgan leaning against the concrete stairwell pillar outside the science building on Tuesday morning, Kristine reversed out of the visitor lot without ever getting out of her sedan. * **The Burton Station Road Property Release:** Rather than letting Tom or David negotiate the remaining lease paperwork on the Portsmouth apartment, **Cassandra** retained a Norfolk real-estate attorney from **Building 33** on Monday, November 29. Within seventy-two hours, the landlord accepted full lump-sum lease termination funds wired directly from Cassandra's credit union account alongside a formal written notice barring any further contact regarding shared tenancy. * **Parallel West Coast Execution:** While the Virginia Beach pack held the physical line, Cassandra spent her evenings in Federal Way executing two quiet miracles simultaneously: filing Liz Carter's spring transfer admission to **Northwest Pacific University** (`3.8` Shenandoah Valley University GPA) and closing all-cash on the `3,800`-square-foot single-story accessible rambler three flat blocks off the **Quantum Campus** in Redmond so the four of them would never have to squeeze into a two-bedroom apartment again. --- ## 2. Permitting the 6:00 PM *Réveillon* Under the Mount Hope Bridge (`December 2004`) Five hundred miles northeast on Aquidneck Island, a completely different logistical meeting unfolded inside **Portsmouth Town Hall** on the first Wednesday of December. For generations, the French-Canadian families clustered along Mussel Bed Shoal Road—anchored by patriarch **Marc-André Bouchard** and his wife **Céline**—had celebrated *Le Réveillon* the traditional Québécois way: gathering *after* Midnight Mass at `1:00 AM` inside cramped, booming dining rooms packed wall-to-wall with forty relatives shouting over fiddles and clattering china until dawn. When **Robert Delaney** walked next door in late November to tell Marc-André that **Erin, Megan, Chloe, and Claire's** Virginia Beach cousins and extended Vance pack—fourteen people total, including three wheelchair users (**Cassandra**, **Kate**, and **David Delaney**) and two teenagers recovering from a brutal autumn (**David** and **Casey Vance**)—were flying into T. F. Green Airport for Christmas week, Marc-André didn't hesitate for a second. "My front steps have four granite risers and a twenty-six-inch parlor doorway," Marc-André noted immediately in his thick Québécois cadence, setting his coffee mug down on the kitchen counter. "We are not leaving three wheelchairs out on the porch, and we are not keeping kids who need their sleep up until two in the morning. We take the feast under the bridge." Together, Marc-André Bouchard and Robert Delaney filed an application with the **Town of Portsmouth** for a neighborhood holiday block-party closure at the foot of Mussel Bed Shoal Road directly beneath the towering concrete-and-steel piers of the **Mount Hope Bridge**: > **Town of Portsmouth — Special Neighborhood Event & Municipal Right-of-Way Permit (`#2004-1224-MBS`)**
> **Applicants:** M. Bouchard & R. Delaney (Mussel Bed Shoal Road Neighborhood Association)
> **Approved Window:** Friday, December 24, 2004 • `5:00 PM – 10:00 PM EST` (Strict `10:00 PM` Municipal Quiet-Hours Cutoff)
> **Barricade Zone:** Dead-end waterfront cul-de-sac beneath the southern suspension piers of the Mount Hope Bridge (Public Works wooden sawhorses staged at `4:30 PM`; full emergency-lane clearance maintained).
> **Accessibility & Safety Stipulations:**
> 1. Twelve commercial-grade stainless-steel outdoor propane patio heaters spaced along the level asphalt apron to maintain a warm microclimate against coastal Narragansett Bay wind.
> 2. Unbolted eight-foot folding banquet tables arranged with forty-eight-inch clear turning aisles for manual and power wheelchairs.
> 3. Zero amplified PA speakers—overhead golden bistro string lights only, preserving neighborhood quiet hours. Neither Marc-André nor Robert had consciously set out to engineer an autism-friendly sensory environment—they simply wanted their neighbors' wheelchairs on flat ground and everyone home in warm beds before midnight. Yet by trading cramped indoor acoustics for open winter air, golden string lights, steaming paper boats of *poutine* and *tourtière*, and the low, rhythmic white-noise hum of tires crossing the green steel bridge grid two hundred feet overhead, the Mussel Bed Shoal neighbors accidentally built one of the safest holiday memories of David and Casey Vance's lives. --- ## Companion Chapters in *The Quantum Directive: The Caretakers* * [**Book 2, Chapter 9, Part 2: *The Twenty-One Day Bridge & The Birthday Buyout* (`November 25–26, 2004`)**](https://books.raggiesoft.com/quantum-directive-3-casey/book-2-the-sovereign-perimeter/chapter-9-the-crossroads/part-2-the-twenty-one-day-bridge-the-birthday-buyout) — Cassandra takes the silver flip phone in David's Virginia Beach bedroom, solves the finals stalemate in twenty minutes, and books a spring mountain fortress called *The Prospector's Keep*. * [**Book 2, Chapter 16: *The Morning Pile & The House Guard Marathon* (`December 24, 2004`)**](https://books.raggiesoft.com/quantum-directive-3-casey/book-2-the-sovereign-perimeter/chapter-16-the-aquidneck-christmas/the-morning-pile-the-house-guard-marathon) — After a cozy Christmas Eve morning pajama pile on the Portsmouth living room sofa, the pack walks down Mussel Bed Shoal Road into the glowing *Réveillon* festival beneath the Mount Hope Bridge.

This Backstage dossier examines Chelsea's landlord-tenant protections in Newport and the two transit rules Brandon Mercer never bothered to read before fleeing Williamsburg.

---

## 1. Cousin Chelsea's Lease Protections on "Dirty Old Tonomy Hill" (`December 24–27, 2004`)

When nineteen-year-old **Katie, Nate, and Heather** and seventeen-year-old **Wesley** rode north up the Eastern Seaboard to **Newport, Rhode Island** for Christmas Eve 2004 after the passing of **Aunt Elizabeth** and **Grandma Ruth**, twenty-two-year-old **Chelsea** welcomed all four of them into her ground-floor Tonomy Hill apartment—forming an immediate, lifelong bond with Wesley over toy city buses and stuffed sea turtle *Shelly*:

1. **Chelsea Was the Sole Named Tenant on the Newport Housing Authority Lease:**
   The ground-floor unit in the World War II-era Tonomy Hill public-housing complex was **100% Cousin Chelsea's apartment**, leased solely in Chelsea's name through her Rhode Island adult developmental-disability caseworker after Aunt Liz passed away. Under Rhode Island landlord-tenant law and Newport Housing Authority guest rules, Chelsea held complete legal authority over who was welcome inside her front door—and only trusted family (`Uncle David, Katie, Nate, Heather, and Wesley`) had their names listed on her caseworker's approved family-visitor sheet.
2. **Why Tonomy Hill's Later Demolition Set Up King's College's 2008 Probate Fraud (`Episode 9, Chapter 4`):**
   When the Newport Housing Authority later demolished the aging Tonomy Hill complex and Chelsea struggled in an unsupported private apartment, King's College's **Regalis Community Living Foundation** in Braxton exploited her move by mailing notice to a house Uncle David had sold in 2001—falsely swearing on `Form PC-2.2` that Chelsea had *"No Known Living Next of Kin"* until David, Katie, Nate, and Brittany tore that perjured order apart in **Braxton Municipal Probate Court** in July 2016.

---

## 2. Two Transit Rules Brandon Mercer Never Bothered to Read (`October 16–17, 2004`)

Two months earlier in Williamsburg, Brandon Mercer prided himself on outsmarting everyone around him—yet his entire October 16 flight collapsed because a controlling abuser knew nothing about how rail tariffs or municipal cross-border transit actually work:

1. **Regular Adult Cash Fares vs. `PWD + Companion` Tariffs:**
   Walking up to the interior **ARTS** counter in Williamsburg ahead of Katie and Nate's Saturday day visit, Brandon bought Regular Adult one-way tickets toward Detroit (`DET`) without realizing rail carriers offer discounted *Passenger with a Disability (`PWD`) + Companion* fares—and without realizing Regular Adult promotional cash fares carry strict forfeiture rules unless exchanged intact at a staffed counter. When he spitefully tore Katie's unused ticket and purchase receipt in half on **East Jefferson Avenue** in Detroit before boarding the **Transit Windsor Tunnel Bus**, he threw away the only exchange credit that could have gotten him out of Michigan.
2. **Why Taking a City Bus Across an International Border Is *Harder*, Not Easier, Than Cross-Border Rail:**
   Afraid that boarding a direct New York-to-Toronto **ARTS** train would put his name on an advance electronic **CBSA** manifest while carrying two external hard drives full of skimmed credit-card numbers, Brandon assumed a local **Transit Windsor Tunnel Bus** worked like an ordinary city bus hop. In reality, walking into **`555 Goyeau Street`** and **`35 Park Street East`** off the Tunnel Bus with a fifty-pound duffel bag, zero return ticket, `$1.75` left after feeding his last `$10` U.S. bill into a no-change Canadian farebox that rejected American dimes and dollar coins, and printed notes about free **`OHIP`** provincial healthcare triggered an immediate **CBSA Secondary Inspection**—and guaranteed a mandatory warrantless **U.S. CBP** forensic search (`19 U.S.C. § 1582`) of both contraband hard drives the moment the caged CBSA van brought him back to **East Jefferson Avenue and Randolph Street**.

    Afraid that boarding a direct New York-to-Toronto ARTS train would put his name on an advance electronic CBSA manifest while carrying two external hard drives full of skimmed credit-card numbers, Brandon assumed a local Transit Windsor Tunnel Bus worked like an ordinary city bus hop. In reality, walking into 555 Goyeau Street and 35 Park Street East off the Tunnel Bus with a fifty-pound duffel bag, zero return ticket, $1.75 left after feeding his last $10 U.S. bill into a no-change Canadian farebox that rejected American dimes and dollar coins, and printed notes about free OHIP provincial healthcare triggered an immediate CBSA Secondary Inspection—and guaranteed a mandatory warrantless U.S. CBP forensic search (19 U.S.C. § 1582) of both contraband hard drives the moment the caged CBSA van brought him back to East Jefferson Avenue and Randolph Street.
