Katie's and Nate's jaws drop open in unison as Wesley—every trace of anger gone from his face—beams with pure triumphant joy, fishes his blue silicone ring back out of his khaki pocket, drops to one knee on the linoleum beside the stage curtain, and gives Nate's knuckles two proud, emphatic taps!

"Way to go, Wes!" Katie gasps, half-laughing through her bandaged nose as she reaches out to squeeze Wesley's forearm with both hands.

Behind them in the hallway, the Night Supervisor's face cycles from chalk-white to deep purple as he stammers weakly toward Lieutenant Miller, "H-he still damaged the front-door strike plate on a state building—"

Lieutenant Miller turns his head slowly, looks from Katie's bandaged nose to Heather's 10:44 PM text timestamp to the 1:00 AM Missing Vulnerable Adult Incident Sheet clipped to the Night Supervisor's own board, and shuts him down ice-cold:

"Let me make sure I understand you for my Sheriff's report. You initiated a county-wide missing-vulnerable-adult emergency for an injured young woman, signed a state log claiming this closet was empty without turning the light switch on, refused to check the exact room sitting on her number-one emergency contact's phone, and you want me to charge the one young man on this campus who actually rescued her under Virginia emergency necessity?! Be grateful all he popped loose was four worn-out screws on a 1974 latch plate—because her father is still driving down Interstate 81 from Alexandria!"

Dr. Evelyn Cross closes her eyes and doesn't utter another syllable about the door.

4. The Legal Breakdown: Why the Sheriff's Lieutenant Could Not (and Would Not) Arrest Wesley

Why does Lieutenant Miller immediately shut down RRC's demand to arrest Wesley—even though Wesley popped the Rec Hall strike plate loose right in front of a uniformed deputy? Under Commonwealth of Virginia law in 2007, four interlocking rules protect Wesley on the spot:

  1. Common-Law Defense of Necessity (Va. Code § 1-200; Humphrey v. Commonwealth, 37 Va. App. 36):
    Virginia preserves the common-law necessity justification whenever minor property damage or entry is committed to prevent a greater imminent harm. Every required legal element happens right in front of Lieutenant Miller:
    • Reasonable Belief of Imminent Harm: RRC itself declared an active Missing Vulnerable Adult emergency for two full-time wheelchair users, one of whom (Katie) suffered acute facial and nasal trauma hours earlier—carrying real risk of concussion or secondary bleeding inside a locked, unmonitored building with powered-off phones.
    • No Legal Alternative Left: Heather and Wesley tried the lawful route first—driving straight to Barton Hall and showing Dr. Cross and the Night Supervisor Nate's 10:44 PM text naming the exact Rec Hall closet—and RRC staff refused to use their master key.
    • Proportionality ("Lesser of Two Evils"): Popping four oxidized screws out of a worn 1974 latch plate (less than five dollars in hardware) is vastly outweighed by reaching an injured missing vulnerable adult—and the instant the closet opens with Katie and Nate sitting right inside, necessity is proven beyond dispute.
  2. Zero Criminal "Unlawful" Intent Under Va. Code §§ 18.2-137 & 18.2-138:
    Under Virginia's property-damage and public-building statutes (Va. Code § 18.2-137 and § 18.2-138), damaging property is only a crime when done "unlawfully"—meaning with criminal or vandalism intent (mens rea), not a good-faith rescue during an active missing-persons alert. Even if someone tried to classify pulling a worn strike plate loose without intent to vandalize under § 18.2-137(A), repair cost well below $1,000 (literally two #10 sheet-metal screws) is at most a Class 3 misdemeanor carrying zero authorized jail time and subject to statutory dismissal once repair costs are satisfied.
  3. Virginia's Mandatory Misdemeanor Summons Rule (Va. Code § 19.2-74) Prohibits Custodial Arrest:
    When panicked staff shout "Arrest him right now!", they assume police can handcuff and haul someone to jail over a broken latch. In Virginia, Va. Code § 19.2-74 legally prohibits taking a person into physical custodial arrest for a Class 1, 2, 3, or 4 misdemeanor unless the person refuses to stop the act or poses an ongoing danger. Once Wesley opens the closet door and kneels peacefully beside Nate, Lieutenant Miller has zero legal authority to place Wesley in handcuffs even if he wanted to.
  4. Probable-Cause Discretion & RRC's Catastrophic Courtroom Exposure:
    State agency administrators cannot order a Sheriff's officer to make an arrest—probable cause belongs solely to law enforcement and the Augusta County Commonwealth's Attorney. No prosecutor in Virginia would ever bring a case against a non-verbal autistic young adult who rescued two "missing" disabled students from the exact locked building RRC falsely certified on a 1:00 AM state incident form was empty—especially when walking into a courtroom would put RRC under oath regarding Tuesday afternoon's unnotified pool battery and a falsified state Missing Vulnerable Adult clearance log.

5. 1:45 AM – 8:30 AM — Calling Dad on I-81, Two Hardware-Store Screws, & Saving Natalie

Rescuing Katie and Nate at 1:35 AM—more than two full hours earlier than in Ending B—makes the rest of Wednesday morning even sweeter:

  1. 1:45 AM — Calling David Before He Even Passes Strasburg (Plus Filing Criminal Charges Against Chris):
    Thirty-five minutes into David Prairie's two-and-a-half-hour haul from Alexandria—right where I-66 West meets I-81 South—David's truck cab fills with laughter and relief when Heather calls on speakerphone: "Mr. Prairie, take your foot off the gas and cruise safe—Wesley got mad when staff wouldn't believe Nate's text, yanked the Rec Hall door lock clean loose himself, and pulled Katie and Nate right out of the closet! Lieutenant Miller is taking Katie's criminal assault statement against Christopher Vance right now!"
    With Lieutenant Miller already standing inside the Rec Hall, Katie and Nate sign a formal criminal battery complaint before 2:10 AM (putting Christopher Vance in Augusta County handcuffs at 7:00 AM and completely preventing Wednesday night's attack on classmate Natalie), and Heather and Wesley drive Katie and Nate back to Room 114 in Waynesboro by 2:25 AM so the twins are already tucked safely into the hotel suite's carpeted walk-in closet when David rolls in at 3:45 AM!
  2. 8:15 AM — Hero Handshakes for Wesley, $0.38 in Screws, & Tina's PHP / SQL Thumb Drive:
    After greeting Wesley at the hotel with the proudest bear-hug handshake of Wesley's life, David drives back onto the sunny RRC campus at 8:15 AM alongside Heather, Wesley, Katie, and Nate to load their Barton Hall suitcases into his pickup. Walking up to the front counter, David calmly sets two brand-new #10 stainless-steel sheet-metal screws from a thirty-eight-cent Waynesboro hardware packet squarely onto Dr. Cross's blotter ("For your 1974 Rec Hall strike plate—keep the change"), before classmate Tina hurries out of the Dining Hall breezeway laughing in pure awe at hearing how Heather's quiet cousin single-handedly defeated a state lock and presses a 2-gigabyte USB drive containing the rest of the Web Applications Developer (PHP & SQL) curriculum straight into Katie's hand as all five roll out of Fishersville together.

markdown:
> **Archival Note:** In [**`Alternate 'What If' — Ending A (1:35 AM)`**](/books/katie/what-if-rrc-unlocked-closet-ending-a-wesley-breaks-the-door), angry **Wesley** refuses to let staff call Nate a liar and yanks the locked Rec Hall door open himself two hours before **David Prairie** arrives.
>
> This **Alternate 'What If' Dossier (`Ending B — 3:50 AM`)**—paired with [**`Ending A — 1:35 AM`**](/books/katie/what-if-rrc-unlocked-closet-ending-a-wesley-breaks-the-door) and [**`Ending C — 6:40 AM`**](/books/katie/what-if-rrc-unlocked-closet-ending-c-six-forty-am-stealth)—explores what happens if Heather keeps Wesley seated calmly outside Barton Hall for two hours while RRC pulls its `"Parent/Guardian Only"` card, until **David Prairie** arrives from Alexandria at `3:45 AM` and asks whether anyone actually flipped the closet light switch on.

---

## 1. 10:44 PM – 11:26 PM — Texting Heather, Shutting Their Phones Off, & The Unlocked-Door Camouflage

At `10:44 PM` on Tuesday night, July 17, 2007—five hours after classmate **Christopher Vance** struck Katie across the face in the ninety-two-degree therapeutic pool and Student Health taped sterile wound-closure strips and white gauze across the split bridge of her nose—Nate and Katie slip down the darkened rear corridor of the **Campus Recreation Hall** in their dry jeans, sneakers, and zip-up fleece hoodies.

Under RRC's **`Level 2` Pass System**, overnighting off campus *was* allowed, **but** it had to be approved in advance by their vocational counselor (who had already left for the day and was off work Wednesday) **and** the person picking them up had to be a **Parent or Legal Guardian**—ruling out **Heather Collins** five minutes down Route 250 in Waynesboro while **David Prairie** lived two and a half hours north in Alexandria.

Rolling their two collapsible black cross-brace manual wheelchairs (outfitted with right-armrest joysticks and removable under-seat battery packs while their heavy `SwiftChairs` stay home in Virginia Beach) inside the deep walk-in seasonal storage closet, Nate reaches back to twist the brass interior thumb-turn lock.

In this timeline, Katie catches his wrist in the dark before the bolt can click.

"Wait a second, Nate—don't lock it!" Katie whispers past the white medical tape across her nose, her analytical brain connecting nine days of dining-hall gossip in a flash. "Why was this closet door unlocked when we just turned the knob? Maintenance leaves it unlocked! Every couple on campus who sneaks off to hook up locks the door behind them—if a staffer checks the hallway and feels a locked storage door, they'll pull out a master key in two seconds! Leave it unlocked, fold our chairs flat behind the winter-coat racks, and get behind the stage curtains!"

Moving with quiet twin teamwork in the cedar-scented dark:
1. Before shutting their flip phones completely **OFF** so no stray text chime, vibration, or low-battery chirp can give away their hiding spot, Nate flips open his phone inside his hoodie and texts **Heather**: <sms>A guy in our class hit Katie's nose in the pool today. Clinic patched her up and she's okay, just shaken up and doesn't want to be alone tonight. We're hiding in the seasonal storage closet at the end of the back hallway in the Rec Hall to sleep. Shutting both our phones completely off now so nobody hears them. If this doesn't work tonight, tomorrow we're sleeping at the hotel with you and Wesley. Love you.</sms> Neither twin feels the slightest bit awkward telling Heather they are hiding in a closet—because Heather already knows they sleep side by side in their bedroom closet at home. Both twins then hold down their red power keys until both phones power completely down to black.
2. They unclip both under-seat battery boxes, **collapse both cross-brace joystick wheelchair frames flat**, and slide them completely out of sight behind a waist-high row of lumpy canvas winter-coat bags.
3. Behind the coat racks in the far back corner, they arrange two soft foam bundles on the linoleum, drape a heavy folded burgundy velvet stage curtain over their shoulders against the building's chilly overnight air conditioning, and wrap their arms tightly around each other.

At **`11:25 PM`**, footsteps echo down the rear Rec Hall corridor right on schedule after Barton Hall's `11:00 PM` curfew check finds both of their dorm beds empty.

Katie and Nate hold their breath behind the stage curtains.

Outside, the **Night Supervisor** grabs the brass doorknob expecting the telltale resistance of two students locked inside. Instead, the knob turns effortlessly. He cracks the door six inches without bothering to reach inside for the wall switch, sweeps a lazy half-second flashlight beam across the empty front linoleum and dusty canvas coat bags—seeing zero people and zero wheelchairs—mutters *"Nobody in the closet either—come on, let's check Cantor Hall,"* pulls the door shut, and **locks the outer Rec Hall doors for the night**.

Under the velvet curtain, Katie and Nate exchange a silent, triumphant squeeze in the dark and drift peacefully off to sleep—100% convinced that the absolute worst thing happening across the courtyard in Barton Hall is a dorm aide checking *Absent at 11:00 PM Curfew Check* on tomorrow morning's clipboard.

---

## 2. 11:30 PM – 3:45 AM — Heather & Wesley Arrive in 9 Minutes; David Drives 2.5 Hours From Alexandria

Across the grass in **Barton Hall**, however, *not* catching Katie and Nate in the Rec Hall at `11:25 PM` turns the Night Supervisor's evening into a five-alarm institutional nightmare:

* **Midnight — Every Building, Walkway, & `9:30 PM` SVT Bus Log Comes Up Empty:**
  Staff sweep Cantor Hall's lounges, the Bates-Harding breezeways, the gazebo, and the parking lots, and double-check the evening bus check-in sheet from the on-campus **Shenandoah Valley Transit (`SVT`)** shelter. Under RRC's Level 2 Pass policy, staff met the final **`9:30 PM` Route 250 Connector** trips arriving from Waynesboro (`9:51 PM`) and Staunton (`10:00 PM`, reaching their opposite terminals by `10:30 PM`) to check returning clients in, and SVT Dispatch reported zero late or broken-down buses. Neither twin drives, and neither had an approved Overnight Pass on file. Outside the gates runs unlit, sidewalk-free **U.S. Route 250** in humid July darkness, where tractor-trailers barrel past gravel ditches at fifty-five miles per hour.
* **1:10 AM — Waking Both Waynesboro (`9 Minutes Away`) and Alexandria (`2 Hours 30 Minutes Away`):**
  Under state rehabilitation regulations, two full-time wheelchair users unaccounted for past `11:00 PM` curfew check—one treated at `7:30 PM` for an acute facial and nasal injury—trigger Mandatory Missing Vulnerable Adult notifications before calling the **Augusta County Sheriff's Office** and **Virginia State Police**. At `1:10 AM`, **Center Director Dr. Evelyn Cross** calls both **Priority Emergency Contact #1 Heather Collins** (at the extended-stay hotel near the Waynesboro ValueMart, roughly **seven miles / eight to ten minutes** east via `I-64` Exit 94 to Exit 91) and **Parent David Prairie** (on Sunset Drive in Alexandria, roughly **155 miles / two hours and thirty minutes** north via `I-66 West`, `I-81 South`, and `I-64 East` Exit 91)—forcing Dr. Cross to stammer to David both that *a male student injured Katie's nose in the pool that afternoon without anyone notifying him*, and that *both twins are missing*.
  With both twins' flip phones powered completely **OFF** inside the closet, calls to Katie and Nate go straight to voicemail.
* **1:12 AM – 1:20 AM — Heather Calms Wesley, Reassures David on `I-66`, & Pulls Onto Campus in Nine Minutes:**
  Woken out of a sound sleep in **Room 114** near the Waynesboro ValueMart, Heather flips open her cell phone and immediately sees **Nate's `10:44 PM` text message** sitting on her screen! When **Wesley** sits bolt upright in the adjacent queen bed turning his blue silicone ring rapidly in middle-of-the-night alarm, Heather angles her phone toward his eyes and steadies him in ten seconds flat: *"Deep breath, Wes—Katie and Nate aren't lost! Nate texted me at ten-forty-four—somebody hurt Katie's nose in the pool today, so they hid together in the storage closet at the back of the Rec Hall with their phones shut off, just like their closet at home!"*
  Dialing David's cell at `1:14 AM` right as David roars onto `I-66 West` out of Alexandria in his Crew Cab pickup, Heather spares him two and a half hours of highway terror (*"Mr. Prairie, drive safe—they're NOT on the highway! Nate texted me they're asleep in the Rec Hall seasonal closet with their phones shut off! Wes and I will be at Barton Hall in eight minutes!"*). Furious that RRC hid Katie's pool injury from him all afternoon, David stays right on `I-66 West` toward `I-81 South` for the two-and-a-half-hour haul while Heather and Wesley hop into Heather's silver accessible van and pull through RRC's front gates at **`1:20 AM`**—just **nine minutes** after Dr. Cross's phone call.
* **1:20 AM – 3:45 AM — Two Hours of Peak Bureaucratic Stubbornness While Waiting for Dad:**
  Walking straight into Barton Hall at `1:20 AM` with Wesley calmly at her side, Heather holds Nate's `10:44 PM` text up to **Dr. Cross** and the **Night Supervisor**. Instead of thanking her and walking sixty yards across the grass, RRC staff pull the **exact same bureaucratic `"Parent/Guardian Only"` card** from Sunday check-in: insisting that the Night Supervisor *"already checked that seasonal closet at 11:25 PM and found the door unlocked and empty,"* brushing off Nate's `10:44 PM` text as an old message sent before leaving campus, and refusing to unlock a closed campus building at `1:30 AM` on the word of *"someone who is neither a parent nor a legal guardian!"*
  Even as **Augusta County Sheriff's Lieutenant Miller** and **Virginia State Police** units comb `U.S. Route 250` between Staunton and Waynesboro for the next two hours, Heather sits calmly with Wesley on the warm brick bench outside Barton Hall—telling Lieutenant Miller with quiet certainty: *"They sleep in their bedroom walk-in closet at home every single night, Lieutenant. The minute Mr. Prairie finishes driving down I-81 from Alexandria and makes them turn that light switch on, you're going to find both of them under a curtain."*

---

## 3. 3:45 AM – 4:15 AM — Dad Arrives From Alexandria, Flips the Switch, & *"Who Went Missing?!"*

At **`3:45 AM`**—two hours and thirty minutes after pulling out of Alexandria—David's pickup rumbles through the front gates off Route 250 and parks right beside Heather's van, two **Augusta County Sheriff's** cruisers, and a **Virginia State Police** sedan outside Barton Hall.

Now the legal parent **is** standing on the bricks. Stepping straight up beside Heather and Wesley—who have been waiting patiently on campus for over two hours—David glances once at Nate's `10:44 PM` text on Heather's phone and locks eyes with the Night Supervisor with calm systems-engineer precision:

> *"Heather drove over here from Waynesboro in nine minutes two hours ago and handed you the exact room my son texted her. Let me ask you one question: at eleven-twenty-five, did you walk inside that closet, flip the wall light switch on, and look behind the winter-coat racks—or did you crack an unlocked door six inches in the dark?"*

The Night Supervisor's sudden two-second silence tells Lieutenant Miller everything he needs to know.

At **`3:50 AM`**, keys jingle down the silent rear corridor of the Rec Hall. David opens the unlocked solid-wood closet door wide, reaches inside to flip the wall toggle switch **ON**, and steps back half a pace beside Heather, Wesley, and Lieutenant Miller as the warm sixty-watt ceiling bulb floods the storage room.

In the back corner behind the winter-coat bags—right beside two neatly folded black joystick wheelchairs—Katie and Nate, wrapped to the chin in a burgundy velvet stage curtain, scrunch their eyes shut against the sudden light, blink three times, and sit up groggily in their hoodies, jeans, and sneakers.

Having slept soundly for five hours with their phones powered completely off, **neither Katie nor Nate has the slightest clue that anyone on earth thinks they are missing.**

Rubbing his eyes in total bewilderment, Nate stares past a uniformed county sheriff's badge at his father—standing 155 miles from Alexandria—right alongside Heather and Wesley at ten minutes to four in the morning.

"Dad?! Heather?! Wes?!" Nate blurts out, completely baffled. "What are all of you doing in a closet in Fishersville at four in the morning?! Wait—why is the Sheriff here? Did somebody go missing on campus?!"

Beside him, Katie blinks innocently past the white gauze strip across her nose, looking anxiously from Lieutenant Miller's flashlight to Heather and Dr. Cross in the hallway. "Did somebody run away from Barton Hall? Wait, Heather—didn't you get Nate's text?!"

For two full seconds nobody in that doorway can speak—until David lets out a ragged half-laugh, half-exhale that takes twenty years off his chest, drops straight to both knees on the linoleum beside the stage curtain, and pulls both of his bewildered twins into a fierce two-armed hug while Heather laughs in pure relief, Wesley steps forward to give Nate's knuckles two joyful taps, and Lieutenant Miller clicks off his flashlight with a sideways grin at the beet-red Night Supervisor.

"Oh, Heather got your text all right—she and Wesley have been sitting outside Barton Hall since one-twenty in the morning trying to tell these folks which closet to open!" Lieutenant Miller chuckles, tipping his hat back an inch. "Half the Augusta County Sheriff's Office and the Virginia State Police have been combing Route 250 looking for **the two of you** while we waited two and a half hours for your dad to get down I-81 and flip the light switch on!"

Katie and Nate stare at each other with their mouths hanging open: *"US?! We were sixty yards across the grass taking a nap!"*

---

## 4. Wednesday Morning Aftermath: Pressing Criminal Charges, Resting at Room 114, & Saving Natalie by Accident

Once the sheer comedy of waking up inside their own missing-persons search settles—and David and Heather get a close look under the ceiling bulb at the purple bruising and `MedStrip` tape across Katie's nose—every trace of humor leaves David Prairie's face.

Because **Augusta County Sheriff's Lieutenant Miller is already standing right inside the building**, Dr. Evelyn Cross has zero opportunity to bury Tuesday afternoon's natatorium assault in an internal administrative file:
1. **Criminal Arrest at Daybreak (`Preventing Wednesday Night's Attack on Natalie`):** Right there in the Rec Hall lobby at `4:15 AM`, Katie and Nate give Lieutenant Miller a sworn criminal complaint detailing **Christopher Vance's** unprovoked battery and destruction of Katie's swimsuit top in the therapeutic pool—plus the poolside staffer's threat to write Nate up for shielding his sister's chest until someone brought a towel. With David demanding formal charges on the spot, Augusta County deputies arrest Christopher Vance in Barton Hall at `7:00 AM` Wednesday morning—meaning Vance is sitting in the Augusta County jail long before Wednesday evening, **inadvertently sparing cognitively vulnerable classmate Natalie from the horrific Wednesday-night scrambled-keycard assault** that occurs in main canon ([***Episode 7, Chapter 3, Part 1***](https://books.raggiesoft.com/katie/fourteen-days-at-roosevelt-rehabilitation-center-two-weeks-in-the-shenandoah-valley-a-secular-wedding-in-2008/ditching-campus-for-the-hotel-room-without-passes-natalie-s-tears-spending-week-two-exploring-the-shenandoah-valley/part-1-the-dormitory-room-mix-up-staying-at-heather-and-wesley-s-hotel-without-passes-natalie-s-tears-outside-the-cafeteria))!
2. **Catching Three Hours of Real Rest at Heather & Wesley's Hotel Before Packing Up (`With Tina's Thumb Drive`):** Refusing to let his twins spend even the rest of dawn under Barton Hall's roof—just as Nate's `10:44 PM` text had promised—David, Heather, and Wesley bring Katie and Nate five minutes down Route 250 to **Room 114** of Heather and Wesley's extended-stay hotel to catch three quiet hours of sleep and hot breakfast together. At `8:15 AM` Wednesday (`Day 11` instead of `Day 13`), when they roll back to Barton Hall to load their suitcases into Dad's pickup, sharp-eyed classmate **Tina** hurries across the sunny July walkway before Mr. Alderman's `8:30 AM` class, grins through her glasses at hearing how an unlocked doorknob and a `10:44 PM` text message humbled the entire Bates-Harding administration, and presses a `2-gigabyte` USB thumb drive containing the entire rest of the **Web Applications Developer (`PHP` & `SQL`)** curriculum straight into Katie's palm before the whole family caravans out of Fishersville for good.

    Under state rehabilitation regulations, two full-time wheelchair users unaccounted for past 11:00 PM curfew check—one treated at 7:30 PM for an acute facial and nasal injury—trigger Mandatory Missing Vulnerable Adult notifications before calling the Augusta County Sheriff's Office and Virginia State Police. At 1:10 AM, Center Director Dr. Evelyn Cross calls both Priority Emergency Contact #1 Heather Collins (at the extended-stay hotel near the Waynesboro ValueMart, roughly seven miles / eight to ten minutes east via I-64 Exit 94 to Exit 91) and Parent David Prairie (on Sunset Drive in Alexandria, roughly 155 miles / two hours and thirty minutes north via I-66 West, I-81 South, and I-64 East Exit 91)—forcing Dr. Cross to stammer to David both that a male student injured Katie's nose in the pool that afternoon without anyone notifying him, and that both twins are missing.
    With both twins' flip phones powered completely OFF inside the closet, calls to Katie and Nate go straight to voicemail.
  • 1:12 AM – 1:20 AM — Heather Calms Wesley, Reassures David on I-66, & Pulls Onto Campus in Nine Minutes:
    Woken out of a sound sleep in Room 114 near the Waynesboro ValueMart, Heather flips open her cell phone and immediately sees Nate's 10:44 PM text message sitting on her screen! When Wesley sits bolt upright in the adjacent queen bed turning his blue silicone ring rapidly in middle-of-the-night alarm, Heather angles her phone toward his eyes and steadies him in ten seconds flat: "Deep breath, Wes—Katie and Nate aren't lost! Nate texted me at ten-forty-four—somebody hurt Katie's nose in the pool today, so they hid together in the storage closet at the back of the Rec Hall with their phones shut off, just like their closet at home!"
    Dialing David's cell at 1:14 AM right as David roars onto I-66 West out of Alexandria in his Crew Cab pickup, Heather spares him two and a half hours of highway terror ("Mr. Prairie, drive safe—they're NOT on the highway! Nate texted me they're asleep in the Rec Hall seasonal closet with their phones shut off! Wes and I will be at Barton Hall in eight minutes!"). Furious that RRC hid Katie's pool injury from him all afternoon, David stays right on I-66 West toward I-81 South for the two-and-a-half-hour haul while Heather and Wesley hop into Heather's silver accessible van and pull through RRC's front gates at 1:20 AM—just nine minutes after Dr. Cross's phone call.
  • 1:20 AM – 3:45 AM — Two Hours of Peak Bureaucratic Stubbornness While Waiting for Dad:
    Walking straight into Barton Hall at 1:20 AM with Wesley calmly at her side, Heather holds Nate's 10:44 PM text up to Dr. Cross and the Night Supervisor. Instead of thanking her and walking sixty yards across the grass, RRC staff pull the exact same bureaucratic "Parent/Guardian Only" card from Sunday check-in: insisting that the Night Supervisor "already checked that seasonal closet at 11:25 PM and found the door unlocked and empty," brushing off Nate's 10:44 PM text as an old message sent before leaving campus, and refusing to unlock a closed campus building at 1:30 AM on the word of "someone who is neither a parent nor a legal guardian!"
    Even as Augusta County Sheriff's Lieutenant Miller and Virginia State Police units comb U.S. Route 250 between Staunton and Waynesboro for the next two hours, Heather sits calmly with Wesley on the warm brick bench outside Barton Hall—telling Lieutenant Miller with quiet certainty: "They sleep in their bedroom walk-in closet at home every single night, Lieutenant. The minute Mr. Prairie finishes driving down I-81 from Alexandria and makes them turn that light switch on, you're going to find both of them under a curtain."

3. 3:45 AM – 4:15 AM — Dad Arrives From Alexandria, Flips the Switch, & "Who Went Missing?!"

At 3:45 AM—two hours and thirty minutes after pulling out of Alexandria—David's pickup rumbles through the front gates off Route 250 and parks right beside Heather's van, two Augusta County Sheriff's cruisers, and a Virginia State Police sedan outside Barton Hall.

Now the legal parent is standing on the bricks. Stepping straight up beside Heather and Wesley—who have been waiting patiently on campus for over two hours—David glances once at Nate's 10:44 PM text on Heather's phone and locks eyes with the Night Supervisor with calm systems-engineer precision:

"Heather drove over here from Waynesboro in nine minutes two hours ago and handed you the exact room my son texted her. Let me ask you one question: at eleven-twenty-five, did you walk inside that closet, flip the wall light switch on, and look behind the winter-coat racks—or did you crack an unlocked door six inches in the dark?"

The Night Supervisor's sudden two-second silence tells Lieutenant Miller everything he needs to know.

At 3:50 AM, keys jingle down the silent rear corridor of the Rec Hall. David opens the unlocked solid-wood closet door wide, reaches inside to flip the wall toggle switch ON, and steps back half a pace beside Heather, Wesley, and Lieutenant Miller as the warm sixty-watt ceiling bulb floods the storage room.

In the back corner behind the winter-coat bags—right beside two neatly folded black joystick wheelchairs—Katie and Nate, wrapped to the chin in a burgundy velvet stage curtain, scrunch their eyes shut against the sudden light, blink three times, and sit up groggily in their hoodies, jeans, and sneakers.

Having slept soundly for five hours with their phones powered completely off, neither Katie nor Nate has the slightest clue that anyone on earth thinks they are missing.

Rubbing his eyes in total bewilderment, Nate stares past a uniformed county sheriff's badge at his father—standing 155 miles from Alexandria—right alongside Heather and Wesley at ten minutes to four in the morning.

"Dad?! Heather?! Wes?!" Nate blurts out, completely baffled. "What are all of you doing in a closet in Fishersville at four in the morning?! Wait—why is the Sheriff here? Did somebody go missing on campus?!"

Beside him, Katie blinks innocently past the white gauze strip across her nose, looking anxiously from Lieutenant Miller's flashlight to Heather and Dr. Cross in the hallway. "Did somebody run away from Barton Hall? Wait, Heather—didn't you get Nate's text?!"

For two full seconds nobody in that doorway can speak—until David lets out a ragged half-laugh, half-exhale that takes twenty years off his chest, drops straight to both knees on the linoleum beside the stage curtain, and pulls both of his bewildered twins into a fierce two-armed hug while Heather laughs in pure relief, Wesley steps forward to give Nate's knuckles two joyful taps, and Lieutenant Miller clicks off his flashlight with a sideways grin at the beet-red Night Supervisor.

"Oh, Heather got your text all right—she and Wesley have been sitting outside Barton Hall since one-twenty in the morning trying to tell these folks which closet to open!" Lieutenant Miller chuckles, tipping his hat back an inch. "Half the Augusta County Sheriff's Office and the Virginia State Police have been combing Route 250 looking for the two of you while we waited two and a half hours for your dad to get down I-81 and flip the light switch on!"

Katie and Nate stare at each other with their mouths hanging open: "US?! We were sixty yards across the grass taking a nap!"

4. Wednesday Morning Aftermath: Pressing Criminal Charges, Resting at Room 114, & Saving Natalie by Accident

Once the sheer comedy of waking up inside their own missing-persons search settles—and David and Heather get a close look under the ceiling bulb at the purple bruising and MedStrip tape across Katie's nose—every trace of humor leaves David Prairie's face.

Because Augusta County Sheriff's Lieutenant Miller is already standing right inside the building, Dr. Evelyn Cross has zero opportunity to bury Tuesday afternoon's natatorium assault in an internal administrative file:

  1. Criminal Arrest at Daybreak (Preventing Wednesday Night's Attack on Natalie): Right there in the Rec Hall lobby at 4:15 AM, Katie and Nate give Lieutenant Miller a sworn criminal complaint detailing Christopher Vance's unprovoked battery and destruction of Katie's swimsuit top in the therapeutic pool—plus the poolside staffer's threat to write Nate up for shielding his sister's chest until someone brought a towel. With David demanding formal charges on the spot, Augusta County deputies arrest Christopher Vance in Barton Hall at 7:00 AM Wednesday morning—meaning Vance is sitting in the Augusta County jail long before Wednesday evening, inadvertently sparing cognitively vulnerable classmate Natalie from the horrific Wednesday-night scrambled-keycard assault that occurs in main canon (Episode 7, Chapter 3, Part 1)!
  2. Catching Three Hours of Real Rest at Heather & Wesley's Hotel Before Packing Up (With Tina's Thumb Drive): Refusing to let his twins spend even the rest of dawn under Barton Hall's roof—just as Nate's 10:44 PM text had promised—David, Heather, and Wesley bring Katie and Nate five minutes down Route 250 to Room 114 of Heather and Wesley's extended-stay hotel to catch three quiet hours of sleep and hot breakfast together. At 8:15 AM Wednesday (Day 11 instead of Day 13), when they roll back to Barton Hall to load their suitcases into Dad's pickup, sharp-eyed classmate Tina hurries across the sunny July walkway before Mr. Alderman's 8:30 AM class, grins through her glasses at hearing how an unlocked doorknob and a 10:44 PM text message humbled the entire Bates-Harding administration, and presses a 2-gigabyte USB thumb drive containing the entire rest of the Web Applications Developer (PHP & SQL) curriculum straight into Katie's palm before the whole family caravans out of Fishersville for good.

markdown:
> **Archival Note:** In [**`Alternate 'What If' — Ending A (1:35 AM)`**](/books/katie/what-if-rrc-unlocked-closet-ending-a-wesley-breaks-the-door), angry **Wesley** refuses to wait for grown-ups and yanks the locked Rec Hall door open himself two hours before **David Prairie** arrives; in [**`Ending B (3:50 AM)`**](/books/katie/what-if-rrc-unlocked-closet-ending-b-three-fifty-am), **Heather and Wesley** wait out RRC's bureaucratic stubbornness until David finishes his two-and-a-half-hour drive from Alexandria at `3:45 AM` and asks whether anyone actually flipped the closet light switch on.
>
> In **`Ending C (6:40 AM)`**, one bureaucratic lie tips the night even further into pure comedy gold: to save his own skin after falsifying the `1:00 AM` state incident form, the **Night Supervisor** swears up and down—first to Heather at `1:20 AM`, and again to David and the **Augusta County Sheriff's Office** at `3:45 AM`—that he *personally entered the Rec Hall seasonal closet with a high-beam flashlight and checked behind every coat rack and curtain*, insisting Nate's `10:44 PM` text was a decoy, keeping everyone out of the Rec Hall until dawn, and setting up the greatest accidental stealth exit in Fishersville history.

---

## 1. 1:10 AM – 6:20 AM — Nine Minutes From Waynesboro, 2.5 Hours From Alexandria, & A Signed Lie on the Hood

Just as in **`Ending A`** and **`Ending B`**, right before powering both of their flip phones completely **OFF** inside the unlocked Rec Hall seasonal storage closet at `10:44 PM` Tuesday night, Nate sent an `<sms>` message to **Heather Collins**: telling her that a classmate had hit Katie's nose in the pool, giving their **exact location** (`the seasonal storage closet at the end of the back hallway in the Rec Hall`), letting her know both phones were being shut completely off for the night, and promising that if this didn't work out tonight, tomorrow they would sleep at the hotel with her and **Wesley**—comfortable telling Heather they were hiding in a closet because she already knew they slept in their bedroom closet at home (`while RRC's Level 2 Overnight Pass rules required advance counselor approval plus pickup by a Parent or Legal Guardian, ruling Heather out that evening`).

When the `9:30 PM` **Shenandoah Valley Transit (`SVT`) Route 250 Connector** check-in logs and the `11:00 PM` Barton Hall curfew check both come up empty, **Dr. Evelyn Cross** wakes both **Priority Emergency Contact #1 Heather Collins** (staying near the Waynesboro ValueMart, roughly **seven miles / eight to ten minutes** away) and **Parent David Prairie** (in Alexandria, roughly **155 miles / two hours and thirty minutes** away via `I-66 West`, `I-81 South`, and `I-64 East` Exit 91) at **`1:10 AM`**:

* **`1:20 AM` — Heather & Wesley Arrive in Nine Minutes (`More Than Two Hours Ahead of David`):**
  Reading Nate's `10:44 PM` text the instant she flips open her phone in **Room 114**, Heather calms **Wesley** right away (*"They aren't lost, Wes—Nate texted me they're sleeping in the Rec Hall closet just like their closet at home with their phones turned off!"*), calls **David** on his cell as he merges onto `I-66 West` so he knows the twins aren't hurt on the highway (while furious over Katie's unnotified pool injury, David stays on `I-66` and `I-81` for the full two-and-a-half-hour drive!), and pulls her silver accessible van onto the RRC campus with Wesley at **`1:20 AM`**—just **nine minutes** after her phone rang.
* **`1:20 AM` & `3:45 AM` — The Night Supervisor's Career-Ending Double-Down:**
  When Heather walks into Barton Hall at `1:20 AM`—and again two hours and twenty-five minutes later at **`3:45 AM`** when **David Prairie** finally pulls in from Alexandria—showing **Augusta County Sheriff's Sergeant Holloway** and Dr. Cross Nate's `10:44 PM` text naming the **Rec Hall seasonal storage closet**, the **Night Supervisor** breaks into a cold sweat. On the `1:00 AM` **Missing Vulnerable Adult Incident Sheet** already faxed to Richmond, he signed his legal signature certifying that he *"personally entered the Rec Hall seasonal storage closet with a flashlight at 23:26, checked behind every coat rack and stage curtain, and verified the room 100% empty."*
  Terrified of admitting in front of two police agencies, a furious parent, and his Director that he lied on a state affidavit without ever flipping the light switch on, the Night Supervisor doubles down at full volume—insisting that Nate must have sent that `10:44 PM` text *as a decoy* before slipping off campus!
* **3:50 AM – 6:20 AM — Searching Route 250 While Heather, Wesley, & David Wait for Dawn:**
  Forced by the signed state affidavit to clear off-campus corridors too, Sheriff's deputies and **Virginia State Police** troopers check `U.S. Route 250` between Staunton and Waynesboro, the emergency-room triage desk across the highway, and the `I-81` / `I-64` interchanges until **`6:20 AM`**, when warm golden July sunrise crests the green Blue Ridge Mountains and the cruisers regroup on the curved brick turnaround of the **main RRC quadrangle** beside David's pickup and Heather's accessible van. Having waited on campus since `1:20 AM` with Wesley while David joined them at `3:45 AM`, Heather crosses her arms and repeats calmly: *"Mr. Prairie, Nate does not send decoy texts. The minute somebody unlocks that Rec Hall for the morning shift, they're sitting behind those curtains."*

Sixty yards behind them, tucked cozily behind racks of winter coats and heavy burgundy velvet stage curtains inside the air-conditioned Rec Hall seasonal storage closet, **Katie and Nate Prairie** wake up after **eight uninterrupted hours of the best sleep they have had since leaving Virginia Beach**.

---

## 2. 6:22 AM – 6:39 AM — Operation Speed-One Stealth Inside the Rec Hall

Stretching his shoulders in the quiet dark without hitting a single dorm wall, Nate checks his watch (`6:22 AM`—both of their powered-off flip phones are still zipped inside their pockets so they won't chime inside the building!) and grins across at Katie in the faint grey crack of light beneath the unlocked wooden door.

"Katie," Nate whispers, barely believing their luck, "nobody opened the door all night! We actually pulled it off!"

Before Katie can whisper back, the heavy steel side maintenance door down by the vending machines clanks open. Footsteps shuffle across the waxed game-room tile, accompanied by the rhythmic *squeak-rattle* of a yellow wheeled mop bucket and a portable transistor radio softly playing early-morning Shenandoah country music as **Earl**, the `6:25 AM` weekday custodian, props the front glass vestibule latches unlocked for morning air and starts mopping around the billiard tables.

Katie's blue eyes light up past the white medical gauze strip taped across the bridge of her nose.

"Nate, listen to me," Katie breathes into his ear, thinking purely about outsmarting a Barton Hall curfew clipboard. "Barton Hall knows we weren't in our beds at eleven o'clock, right? Right now they probably think somebody in Cantor Hall hid us, or they have zero proof where we went! Nobody saw us roll in here last night—so if we sneak out of this building right now **without Earl or a single staffer laying eyes on us**, nobody at RRC will *ever* figure out our unlocked-closet trick! We can power our phones on outside, text Heather good morning, and roll straight into the six-forty-five breakfast line like nothing happened!"

Nate grins from ear to ear and gives her a silent thumbs-up. **Operation Speed-One Stealth** is on:

1. **6:26 AM — Erasing Every Trace Inside the Closet:**
   Moving in slow motion so not a zipper clicks, Katie and Nate stand up in their sneakers, fold the heavy burgundy stage curtain along its exact original creases, slide it silently onto the middle steel shelf, and fluff the two canvas winter-coat bags back into line.
2. **6:30 AM — Unfolding Two Wheelchairs Without a Single Squeak:**
   Lifting their two collapsed black cross-brace manual wheelchairs out from behind the coat racks an inch at a time, Nate holds both thumbs over the steel seat-rail joints while pressing down gently so the frames lock open without their usual metallic *clack*. Wrapping their fleece hoodie cuffs around the plastic battery latches to muffle the snap, both twins slide their `24-volt` battery boxes underneath, transfer smoothly into their seats, click their power toggles on, and **turn their right-armrest speed dials all the way counterclockwise to Setting `1`**—slowing their electric hub motors to a near-silent crawl.
3. **6:34 AM — Timing the Mop Bucket:**
   Easing the unlocked closet door open two inches, Nate peeks down the darkened rear corridor toward the sunlit main game room. Twenty feet past the billiard tables, Earl whistles along to his radio, pushes his yellow mop bucket through the propped-open door of the men's restroom, and turns the utility sink faucet on full blast.
4. **6:36 AM — Behind the Ping-Pong Tables & Freezing at the Trophy Case:**
   Nate waves two fingers behind his back. Rolling nose-to-tail at two miles per hour in utter silence, Nate and Katie glide out of the rear corridor, tuck low behind the green folded tops of three tournament ping-pong tables so their heads stay below sightline, and reach the tall oak-and-glass trophy case beside the front vestibule—just as the utility faucet shuts off and Earl steps halfway back to the restroom doorway to grab a roll of brown paper towels off his cart!
   Directly behind the five-foot wooden trophy cabinet, both twins take their fingers completely off their joysticks and don't breathe for six heart-pounding seconds until Earl disappears back inside the tiled restroom humming to the chorus.
5. **6:39 AM — Slipping Out the Front Vestibule Unseen:**
   Pressing the rubber bumper of his front footrest gently against the horizontal brass push-bar of the propped vestibule door so the latch doesn't click, Nate holds the glass door wide for Katie's wheels, follows her smoothly onto the shaded concrete porch, and glides silently down the side brick ramp behind the tall, trimmed green boxwood hedge separating the Rec Hall from the main campus quadrangle.

Not a single soul inside the Recreation Hall ever saw them enter, sleep, or leave.

---

## 3. 6:40 AM — Rounding the Boxwood Hedge Into Dad, Heather, Wesley, & Two Police Agencies

"Zero witnesses," Nate whispers triumphantly as they roll down the brick path behind the boxwood hedge, dialing his speed knob back up to normal cruising speed while Katie suppresses a proud giggle beside him. "Let's see our counselor prove where we—"

Nate's words die in his throat as both wheelchairs glide side by side past the end of the green boxwood hedge into the warm golden `6:40 AM` July sunlight of the main campus quadrangle.

Katie and Nate pull back on their joysticks at the exact same instant, stopping dead on the bricks.

Parked bumper to bumper around the circular brick turnaround between Barton Hall and the Dining Hall—blue roof lightbars pulsing silently against the red-brick walls in the summer dawn—sit **three Augusta County Sheriff's cruisers, two grey-and-blue Virginia State Police cruisers, and two RRC Campus Police sedans**. Gathered around a campus map taped across a cruiser hood stand half a dozen uniformed deputies and troopers, a pale, hollow-eyed **Dr. Evelyn Cross**, a clipboard-clutching **Night Supervisor** with dark circles under his eyes—and, twenty feet to the right beside Dad's pickup truck and Heather's silver accessible van, **their father David Prairie** holding a foam coffee cup right alongside **Heather Collins** and **Wesley**!

Having spent the last twenty minutes sneaking past a janitor with their phones still powered off so they wouldn't get a petty curfew slip, **neither Katie nor Nate has even a microscopic suspicion that this entire law-enforcement task force is here for them.**

"Whoa, Nate," Katie whispers in wide-eyed shock, staring at the police cruisers and the map on the hood. "Somebody must have escaped off campus in the middle of the night! Wait—is that *Dad's* pickup truck AND *Heather's* van?!"

"What on earth are Dad, Heather, and Wes doing on campus at six-forty on a Wednesday morning?!" Nate whispers back, completely mystified.

Rolling casually out across the sunny brick courtyard right behind the semicircle of troopers—looking around the Barton Hall lawn with genuine neighborly curiosity to see what the commotion is about—Nate raises his voice cheerfully over the quiet murmur of police radios:

> **"Dad?! Heather?! Wes?! What are all of you doing here at six-forty in the morning—and who went missing?!"**

Fourteen heads whip around `180 degrees` at the exact same millisecond.

For four full seconds of absolute, pin-drop Shenandoah Valley silence:
* **David Prairie's** jaw drops open so fast he nearly drops his foam cup of black coffee straight onto his shoes.
* **Heather** points straight from the twins to her flip phone to the Night Supervisor without even needing to say *"I told you so,"* while **Wesley** breaks into a huge grin beside her.
* **Dr. Evelyn Cross** grabs the edge of the cruiser fender as if two ghosts just materialized out of the boxwood bushes.
* **The Night Supervisor**—whose signed state certification swearing that *he personally checked behind every coat rack and stage curtain in the Rec Hall seasonal closet with a flashlight* is literally sitting under the Sheriff's Sergeant's elbow on the hood—turns the exact shade of a boiled lobster.
* And **Augusta County Sheriff's Sergeant Holloway** slowly lowers his grease pencil, stares once at Heather's phone, stares once at the Night Supervisor, stares through the glass doors of the Rec Hall fifty feet behind the twins where Earl is still happily mopping the lobby oblivious to the universe, and looks back at Katie and Nate sitting side by side in clean hoodies and jeans.

"Who went missing?!" Sergeant Holloway repeats, fighting for his life not to burst out laughing in front of two State Troopers. "Son, half of Augusta County, the Virginia State Police, and your family have been up since one o'clock this morning looking for **THE TWO OF YOU**—even after Heather showed us your text message naming that exact closet, because *somebody* signed a state form swearing he checked behind every curtain in there with a flashlight!"

Katie and Nate blink in unison, look at each other across their armrests, look at David, Heather, and Wesley striding across the bricks to wrap both of them in hugs and happy knuckle-taps, and look straight at the crimson-faced Night Supervisor.

"Looking for *us*?!" Katie blurts out in total, innocent astonishment, pointing her thumb back over her shoulder toward the Rec Hall behind the hedge. "We didn't leave campus! We were sixty yards right over there asleep behind the stage curtains in the seasonal closet—exact place Nate texted Heather! We only left the door unlocked—didn't anybody turn the light switch on?!"

Watching Sergeant Holloway slowly turn his head back toward the Night Supervisor—*"Checked behind every coat rack and curtain at 23:26, huh?"*—while Dr. Evelyn Cross closes her eyes in pure career-ending agony is a sight neither Katie, Nate, Heather, Wesley, nor David ever forgets for the rest of their lives.

---

## 4. 7:00 AM – 8:45 AM — Criminal Handcuffs for Chris, Tina's Thumb Drive, & Leaving Fishersville Together

Just like in [**`Ending A`**](/books/katie/what-if-rrc-unlocked-closet-ending-a-wesley-breaks-the-door) and [**`Ending B`**](/books/katie/what-if-rrc-unlocked-closet-ending-b-three-fifty-am), having the **Augusta County Sheriff's Office** and **Virginia State Police** standing ten feet away when David and Heather examine Katie's bandaged, bruised nose shatters RRC's ability to sweep Tuesday afternoon's pool assault under the rug:

* **7:15 AM — Arresting Christopher Vance (`Saving Natalie Twelve Hours Early`):** Learning right on the courtyard bricks that **Christopher Vance** struck Katie across the face and ripped her swimsuit top in the therapeutic pool yesterday afternoon—and that nobody at RRC called the police or notified her father until they thought she had vanished—David files an immediate criminal assault-and-battery complaint with Sergeant Holloway. Deputies walk straight into Barton Hall and take Christopher Vance out in handcuffs before breakfast finishes—**preventing Wednesday night's dorm-database keycard attack on cognitively disabled classmate Natalie** before it can ever happen!
* **8:30 AM — Packing Up With a Full Night's Sleep & Tina's `PHP` / `SQL` Drive:** While half of Barton Hall cheers quietly from the second-story windows watching David hoist Katie's and Nate's folded wheelchairs beneath the camper shell of his pickup (`Day 11`) right beside Heather and Wesley's van, classmate **Tina** walks briskly out of the Dining Hall breezeway, adjusts her glasses with a grin of pure admiration at the twins who defeated state bureaucracy with an unlocked doorknob, a `10:44 PM` text to Heather, and Speed Setting `1`, and slips a `2-gigabyte` USB drive packed with the rest of Mr. Alderman's **Web Applications Developer** `PHP` and `SQL` modules straight into Nate's hand before the whole family rolls out of Fishersville free.

On the 1:00 AM Missing Vulnerable Adult Incident Sheet already faxed to Richmond, he signed his legal signature certifying that he "personally entered the Rec Hall seasonal storage closet with a flashlight at 23:26, checked behind every coat rack and stage curtain, and verified the room 100% empty."
    Terrified of admitting in front of two police agencies, a furious parent, and his Director that he lied on a state affidavit without ever flipping the light switch on, the Night Supervisor doubles down at full volume—insisting that Nate must have sent that 10:44 PM text as a decoy before slipping off campus!
  • 3:50 AM – 6:20 AM — Searching Route 250 While Heather, Wesley, & David Wait for Dawn:
    Forced by the signed state affidavit to clear off-campus corridors too, Sheriff's deputies and Virginia State Police troopers check U.S. Route 250 between Staunton and Waynesboro, the emergency-room triage desk across the highway, and the I-81 / I-64 interchanges until 6:20 AM, when warm golden July sunrise crests the green Blue Ridge Mountains and the cruisers regroup on the curved brick turnaround of the main RRC quadrangle beside David's pickup and Heather's accessible van. Having waited on campus since 1:20 AM with Wesley while David joined them at 3:45 AM, Heather crosses her arms and repeats calmly: "Mr. Prairie, Nate does not send decoy texts. The minute somebody unlocks that Rec Hall for the morning shift, they're sitting behind those curtains."

Sixty yards behind them, tucked cozily behind racks of winter coats and heavy burgundy velvet stage curtains inside the air-conditioned Rec Hall seasonal storage closet, Katie and Nate Prairie wake up after eight uninterrupted hours of the best sleep they have had since leaving Virginia Beach.

2. 6:22 AM – 6:39 AM — Operation Speed-One Stealth Inside the Rec Hall

Stretching his shoulders in the quiet dark without hitting a single dorm wall, Nate checks his watch (6:22 AM—both of their powered-off flip phones are still zipped inside their pockets so they won't chime inside the building!) and grins across at Katie in the faint grey crack of light beneath the unlocked wooden door.

"Katie," Nate whispers, barely believing their luck, "nobody opened the door all night! We actually pulled it off!"

Before Katie can whisper back, the heavy steel side maintenance door down by the vending machines clanks open. Footsteps shuffle across the waxed game-room tile, accompanied by the rhythmic squeak-rattle of a yellow wheeled mop bucket and a portable transistor radio softly playing early-morning Shenandoah country music as Earl, the 6:25 AM weekday custodian, props the front glass vestibule latches unlocked for morning air and starts mopping around the billiard tables.

Katie's blue eyes light up past the white medical gauze strip taped across the bridge of her nose.

"Nate, listen to me," Katie breathes into his ear, thinking purely about outsmarting a Barton Hall curfew clipboard. "Barton Hall knows we weren't in our beds at eleven o'clock, right? Right now they probably think somebody in Cantor Hall hid us, or they have zero proof where we went! Nobody saw us roll in here last night—so if we sneak out of this building right now without Earl or a single staffer laying eyes on us, nobody at RRC will ever figure out our unlocked-closet trick! We can power our phones on outside, text Heather good morning, and roll straight into the six-forty-five breakfast line like nothing happened!"

Nate grins from ear to ear and gives her a silent thumbs-up. Operation Speed-One Stealth is on:

  1. 6:26 AM — Erasing Every Trace Inside the Closet:
    Moving in slow motion so not a zipper clicks, Katie and Nate stand up in their sneakers, fold the heavy burgundy stage curtain along its exact original creases, slide it silently onto the middle steel shelf, and fluff the two canvas winter-coat bags back into line.
  2. 6:30 AM — Unfolding Two Wheelchairs Without a Single Squeak:
    Lifting their two collapsed black cross-brace manual wheelchairs out from behind the coat racks an inch at a time, Nate holds both thumbs over the steel seat-rail joints while pressing down gently so the frames lock open without their usual metallic clack. Wrapping their fleece hoodie cuffs around the plastic battery latches to muffle the snap, both twins slide their 24-volt battery boxes underneath, transfer smoothly into their seats, click their power toggles on, and turn their right-armrest speed dials all the way counterclockwise to Setting 1—slowing their electric hub motors to a near-silent crawl.
  3. 6:34 AM — Timing the Mop Bucket:
    Easing the unlocked closet door open two inches, Nate peeks down the darkened rear corridor toward the sunlit main game room. Twenty feet past the billiard tables, Earl whistles along to his radio, pushes his yellow mop bucket through the propped-open door of the men's restroom, and turns the utility sink faucet on full blast.
  4. 6:36 AM — Behind the Ping-Pong Tables & Freezing at the Trophy Case:
    Nate waves two fingers behind his back. Rolling nose-to-tail at two miles per hour in utter silence, Nate and Katie glide out of the rear corridor, tuck low behind the green folded tops of three tournament ping-pong tables so their heads stay below sightline, and reach the tall oak-and-glass trophy case beside the front vestibule—just as the utility faucet shuts off and Earl steps halfway back to the restroom doorway to grab a roll of brown paper towels off his cart!
    Directly behind the five-foot wooden trophy cabinet, both twins take their fingers completely off their joysticks and don't breathe for six heart-pounding seconds until Earl disappears back inside the tiled restroom humming to the chorus.
  5. 6:39 AM — Slipping Out the Front Vestibule Unseen:
    Pressing the rubber bumper of his front footrest gently against the horizontal brass push-bar of the propped vestibule door so the latch doesn't click, Nate holds the glass door wide for Katie's wheels, follows her smoothly onto the shaded concrete porch, and glides silently down the side brick ramp behind the tall, trimmed green boxwood hedge separating the Rec Hall from the main campus quadrangle.

Not a single soul inside the Recreation Hall ever saw them enter, sleep, or leave.

3. 6:40 AM — Rounding the Boxwood Hedge Into Dad, Heather, Wesley, & Two Police Agencies

"Zero witnesses," Nate whispers triumphantly as they roll down the brick path behind the boxwood hedge, dialing his speed knob back up to normal cruising speed while Katie suppresses a proud giggle beside him. "Let's see our counselor prove where we—"

Nate's words die in his throat as both wheelchairs glide side by side past the end of the green boxwood hedge into the warm golden 6:40 AM July sunlight of the main campus quadrangle.

Katie and Nate pull back on their joysticks at the exact same instant, stopping dead on the bricks.

Parked bumper to bumper around the circular brick turnaround between Barton Hall and the Dining Hall—blue roof lightbars pulsing silently against the red-brick walls in the summer dawn—sit three Augusta County Sheriff's cruisers, two grey-and-blue Virginia State Police cruisers, and two RRC Campus Police sedans. Gathered around a campus map taped across a cruiser hood stand half a dozen uniformed deputies and troopers, a pale, hollow-eyed Dr. Evelyn Cross, a clipboard-clutching Night Supervisor with dark circles under his eyes—and, twenty feet to the right beside Dad's pickup truck and Heather's silver accessible van, their father David Prairie holding a foam coffee cup right alongside Heather Collins and Wesley!

Having spent the last twenty minutes sneaking past a janitor with their phones still powered off so they wouldn't get a petty curfew slip, neither Katie nor Nate has even a microscopic suspicion that this entire law-enforcement task force is here for them.

"Whoa, Nate," Katie whispers in wide-eyed shock, staring at the police cruisers and the map on the hood. "Somebody must have escaped off campus in the middle of the night! Wait—is that Dad's pickup truck AND Heather's van?!"

"What on earth are Dad, Heather, and Wes doing on campus at six-forty on a Wednesday morning?!" Nate whispers back, completely mystified.

Rolling casually out across the sunny brick courtyard right behind the semicircle of troopers—looking around the Barton Hall lawn with genuine neighborly curiosity to see what the commotion is about—Nate raises his voice cheerfully over the quiet murmur of police radios:

"Dad?! Heather?! Wes?! What are all of you doing here at six-forty in the morning—and who went missing?!"

Fourteen heads whip around 180 degrees at the exact same millisecond.

For four full seconds of absolute, pin-drop Shenandoah Valley silence:

  • David Prairie's jaw drops open so fast he nearly drops his foam cup of black coffee straight onto his shoes.
  • Heather points straight from the twins to her flip phone to the Night Supervisor without even needing to say "I told you so," while Wesley breaks into a huge grin beside her.
  • Dr. Evelyn Cross grabs the edge of the cruiser fender as if two ghosts just materialized out of the boxwood bushes.
  • The Night Supervisor—whose signed state certification swearing that he personally checked behind every coat rack and stage curtain in the Rec Hall seasonal closet with a flashlight is literally sitting under the Sheriff's Sergeant's elbow on the hood—turns the exact shade of a boiled lobster.
  • And Augusta County Sheriff's Sergeant Holloway slowly lowers his grease pencil, stares once at Heather's phone, stares once at the Night Supervisor, stares through the glass doors of the Rec Hall fifty feet behind the twins where Earl is still happily mopping the lobby oblivious to the universe, and looks back at Katie and Nate sitting side by side in clean hoodies and jeans.

"Who went missing?!" Sergeant Holloway repeats, fighting for his life not to burst out laughing in front of two State Troopers. "Son, half of Augusta County, the Virginia State Police, and your family have been up since one o'clock this morning looking for THE TWO OF YOU—even after Heather showed us your text message naming that exact closet, because somebody signed a state form swearing he checked behind every curtain in there with a flashlight!"

Katie and Nate blink in unison, look at each other across their armrests, look at David, Heather, and Wesley striding across the bricks to wrap both of them in hugs and happy knuckle-taps, and look straight at the crimson-faced Night Supervisor.

"Looking for us?!" Katie blurts out in total, innocent astonishment, pointing her thumb back over her shoulder toward the Rec Hall behind the hedge. "We didn't leave campus! We were sixty yards right over there asleep behind the stage curtains in the seasonal closet—exact place Nate texted Heather! We only left the door unlocked—didn't anybody turn the light switch on?!"

Watching Sergeant Holloway slowly turn his head back toward the Night Supervisor—"Checked behind every coat rack and curtain at 23:26, huh?"—while Dr. Evelyn Cross closes her eyes in pure career-ending agony is a sight neither Katie, Nate, Heather, Wesley, nor David ever forgets for the rest of their lives.

4. 7:00 AM – 8:45 AM — Criminal Handcuffs for Chris, Tina's Thumb Drive, & Leaving Fishersville Together

Just like in Ending A and Ending B, having the Augusta County Sheriff's Office and Virginia State Police standing ten feet away when David and Heather examine Katie's bandaged, bruised nose shatters RRC's ability to sweep Tuesday afternoon's pool assault under the rug:

  • 7:15 AM — Arresting Christopher Vance (Saving Natalie Twelve Hours Early): Learning right on the courtyard bricks that Christopher Vance struck Katie across the face and ripped her swimsuit top in the therapeutic pool yesterday afternoon—and that nobody at RRC called the police or notified her father until they thought she had vanished—David files an immediate criminal assault-and-battery complaint with Sergeant Holloway. Deputies walk straight into Barton Hall and take Christopher Vance out in handcuffs before breakfast finishes—preventing Wednesday night's dorm-database keycard attack on cognitively disabled classmate Natalie before it can ever happen!
  • 8:30 AM — Packing Up With a Full Night's Sleep & Tina's PHP / SQL Drive: While half of Barton Hall cheers quietly from the second-story windows watching David hoist Katie's and Nate's folded wheelchairs beneath the camper shell of his pickup (Day 11) right beside Heather and Wesley's van, classmate Tina walks briskly out of the Dining Hall breezeway, adjusts her glasses with a grin of pure admiration at the twins who defeated state bureaucracy with an unlocked doorknob, a 10:44 PM text to Heather, and Speed Setting 1, and slips a 2-gigabyte USB drive packed with the rest of Mr. Alderman's Web Applications Developer PHP and SQL modules straight into Nate's hand before the whole family rolls out of Fishersville free.

> **Archival Note:** In [***Katie & Nathaniel — Episode 8***](https://books.raggiesoft.com/katie/do-better-ideas-for-cvta-the-kempsville-city-council/do-better-ideas-for-cvta-the-four-bus-mayoral-loop/part-1-does-the-bus-run-calling-out-cvta-s-complacency-the-2008-regional-mayoral-challenge), twenty-two-year-old **Katie** and **Nathaniel Prairie** turn their transit advocacy blog (*Ideas for Coastal Virginia Transit*) and their May 2008 **"Ride the Bus With Us"** Mayoral Challenge into Katie's historic 2010 landslide campaign for the **Kempsville District** seat on the **Virginia Beach City Council**. This Backstage dossier reveals what happened behind closed doors at **CVTA Headquarters (`509 E. 18th Street`)** and inside twenty-two-year incumbent **Councilman Harold Dietz's** imploding war room.

---

## 1. Why CVTA Executive Leadership Blackballed Nate From `TRAC` (`2007–2010`)

When twenty-one-year-old **Nathaniel Prairie** submitted his application for the citizen **Transit Rider Advisory Committee (`TRAC`)** at **`509 E. 18th Street`** in Norfolk, **CVTA Chief Executive Officer Leonard Sterling** and **Chief Operating Officer Richard Halstead** personally flagged his file in the second-floor executive suite:

1. **They Wanted Compliant Ceremonial Riders, Not Software Engineers Reading the NTD Tables:**
   To Sterling and Halstead, `TRAC` existed to rubber-stamp staff fare-increase proposals and clap politely for glossy PowerPoint slides. The last thing they wanted at the advisory table was the co-author of *Ideas for Coastal Virginia Transit*—who was already publishing interactive route maps exposing how CVTA buses ran once every sixty minutes, stopped running at `7:00 PM`, and stranded wheelchair riders at un-signalized six-lane highway crossings without sidewalks.
2. **Cutting the Microphone at Two Minutes (`02:00`):**
   Whenever Nate and Katie rode two buses into Norfolk to speak during the public-comment period at monthly **Transportation District Commission (`TDC`)** board meetings, COO Halstead instructed the board clerk to start the digital countdown clock the instant their power wheelchairs began rolling toward the lectern—and cut their microphone dead at `02:00` sharp.
3. **The November 2010 Boomerang:**
   Neither Sterling nor Halstead ever imagined that blackballing the brother from a volunteer citizen committee in 2008 would result in the sister being elected to the **Virginia Beach City Council** with **`94.1%` of the vote** in November 2010—and appointed by the Mayor two months later as a **voting Commissioner on the CVTA Board of Directors**, where she sat on the raised dais above their heads with no two-minute clock and voted to clean house in the executive suite.

---

## 2. The Political Folklore of the Newtown Road Timetable Cliff & Mayor Myra E. Overton (`1988–2008`)

Why did the four-bus, three-hour loop on **May 14, 2008**—carrying Norfolk Mayor **Paulina Fraim**, Virginia Beach Mayor **Myra E. Overton**, and Portsmouth Mayor **James Holley** alongside Katie and Nate—strike such a raw nerve across Hampton Roads when their bus hit the Norfolk/Virginia Beach city line at **Newtown Road**?

* **The Invisible Municipal Wall at Newtown Road:**
  For decades, **CVTA Route #1** (`Granby Street / Pembroke East`) operated every `15–30 minutes` on the Norfolk side of the city line, while **CVTA Route #20 / #25** (`Virginia Beach Boulevard / Kempsville`) dropped to `60-minute` headways with uncoordinated transfer windows the instant a rider crossed Newtown Road into Virginia Beach.
* **Twenty Years of Saying *"Nobody Rides the Bus Out Here"*:**
  Throughout her twenty years in Virginia Beach municipal politics (`1988–2008`), **Mayor Myra E. Overton** had defended Virginia Beach's skeletal bus funding by claiming at budget hearings that *"suburban residents prefer their cars."* Having to sit in a rigid molded-fiberglass bus seat for forty-two minutes at the Newtown Road transfer stop in the May humidity while twenty-two-year-old Katie and Nate calmly pointed out on a printed schedule that a five-mile trip from Kempsville to City Hall required four hours and two transfers turned the **Newtown Road Timetable Cliff** into instant Tidewater political folklore.

---

## 3. Why Councilman Harold Dietz Left His Podium Empty on `WHRC TV-15`—and Blew Up His Career on `WTGA 790 AM` (`October 2010`)

How did twenty-two-year incumbent **Councilman Harold Dietz** go from a comfortable `+18%` summer lead to losing the Kempsville District **`94.1%` to `5.9%`** on November 2, 2010?

1. **Why Dietz Never RSVPed to the `WHRC TV-15` Debate (`October 19, 2010`):**
   When public television station **`WHRC TV-15`** sent certified debate invitations to both certified Kempsville candidates in September 2010, Dietz's campaign manager advised him to ignore the letter—assuming `WHRC TV-15` would cancel the broadcast if the incumbent didn't confirm, and refusing to *"elevate a twenty-five-year-old kid in a wheelchair who rides the city bus."*
   Instead, `WHRC TV-15` followed strict FCC *bona fide* news event rules: they set up two podiums under the studio lights, placed a `COUNCILMAN HAROLD DIETZ` nameplate on the empty lectern, and gave twenty-five-year-old **Katie Prairie** thirty uninterrupted minutes on live regional television—followed by *The Tidewater Pilot* front-page Metro photograph of Katie and Nate sprinting across four lanes of Independence Boulevard in the dark at `8:24 PM` to catch the last three buses home.
2. **The Internal Track Poll That Triggered the `WTGA 790 AM` Meltdown (`October 27–28, 2010`):**
   Six days after the `WHRC TV-15` broadcast and the front-page *Tidewater Pilot* story, Dietz's campaign pollster delivered a devastating internal tracking poll of 400 likely Kempsville voters:
   * **September 15, 2010:** Dietz `51%` — Prairie `33%` (`Dietz +18%`)
   * **October 12, 2010:** Dietz `46%` — Prairie `38%` (`Dietz +8%`)
   * **October 27, 2010 (*Post-Empty Podium*):** Prairie `44.6%` — Dietz `44.2%` (`Statistical Tie / Margin of Error 0.4%`)
3. **8:15 AM on `WTGA 790 AM` (*The Morning Drive with Chuck & Dave*):**
   Furious, panicked, and sleepless after seeing his twenty-two-year seat evaporate to a `0.4%` margin against a twenty-five-year-old challenger who hadn't bought a single television commercial, Dietz drove to the **`WTGA 790 AM`** studio on Thursday morning, October 28 without his campaign manager—and went on live talk radio to sneer that electing Katie Prairie would *"cost the taxpayers of Virginia Beach tens of thousands of dollars just to tear up the historic mahogany City Council dais at Building 1 to build a custom wheelchair ramp for one girl who doesn't even own a car."*
   Within four hours, every civic league president, military veteran, church pastor, and parent of a child with a disability in Kempsville had heard the clip—turning a `0.4%` race into the most lopsided City Council landslide (`94.1%`) in Virginia Beach history.

markdown:
On the morning of **Wednesday, January 15, 2014**, in [***Book 4, Chapter 2: "The Ground Truth"***](https://books.raggiesoft.com/quantum-directive-3-casey/book-4-the-sovereign-empire/chapter-2-the-ground-truth/part-2-the-shadow-wallet-the-actuarial-risk), **Quantum Corporation** files its historic SEC `Form 8-K` naming thirty-five-year-old **Cassandra Vance** its third Chief Executive Officer—whereupon Cassandra signs for a black titanium **Meridian Obsidian Card**, demolishes Chief Risk Officer **Sterling's** actuarial objection to public buses, and rides **TAPS King County Route 230** down `156th Avenue NE` to spend her afternoon debugging asynchronous routing code with rookie developers in Bellevue. Because **David Vance** remains stationed outside the frosted-glass boardroom doors during the `9:00 AM` formal vote, and because junior engineers in Bellevue only see an inscrutable man in an **Orange Contractor Badge** clip a pulse oximeter onto the new CEO's finger at `2:00 PM`, this dossier preserves the three institutional shocks unfolding behind the scenes that day. --- ## 1. Eighteen Minutes Behind Frosted Glass (`January 15, 2014 • 9:00 AM`) Although **William Keswick** and **Steve Ballantine** had already informed Cassandra in the empty **Building 33 Vault** at `9:30 PM` the night before ([*Chapter 1: "The Deviation"*](https://books.raggiesoft.com/quantum-directive-3-casey/book-4-the-sovereign-empire/chapter-1-the-mandate/the-deviation-the-sovereign-news)), corporate governance required a formal roll-call resolution of Quantum's eleven-member **Board of Directors** at `9:00 AM` sharp before the `8-K` hit the financial wires. Nine directors arrived already aligned behind the founders. Two external directors—Wall Street private-equity veteran **Richard** and legacy consumer-packaged-goods chairwoman **Evelyn**—cleared their throats before the ballot was called. "Nobody in this room questions Cassandra's mastery of the enterprise cloud stack," Richard began carefully, tapping his leather portfolio. "She built the revenue engine keeping our margins vertical. My concern is Wall Street's opening-bell optics. She just turned thirty-five in November. Every institutional fund manager in Manhattan is expecting a fifty-five-year-old Fortune 50 statesperson." "And there is the cultural posture," Evelyn added, glancing out the fifth-floor glass toward the central campus commons. "When I walked in from the visitor car service twenty minutes ago, half the engineers in **Building 16** told me they call her the *Courtyard CEO* because she sits at outdoor picnic tables in denim jeans with her laptop bolted to her wheelchair—and carries a **MagnaByte mPhone** in her blazer pocket. If financial television catches Quantum's incoming CEO pulling our rival's flagship phone out at a bus shelter, how does Communications spin that?" Steve Ballantine didn't shout.
